summary: The Guardian editorial notes that Ordnance Survey is marking the 225th anniversary of its first publication. It recalls that the 1801 OS map of Kent required ten years to produce, driven by military concerns over a possible Napoleonic invasion.
author: Guardian Science

title: Baxdrostat shows blood pressure benefits lasting up to two years after use
content:
A new medication, baxdrostat, has shown unusually lasting effects on high‑blood‑pressure patients.  In a six‑ to 12‑month daily‑pill regimen, patients’ blood pressure improved, and the benefits persisted for up to two years after they stopped taking the drug.  

Doctors report that some patients no longer required any hypertension drugs and may have been cured of the condition, a result that has “stunned” clinicians.  The drug is said to reverse a common cause of high blood pressure, offering a potential long‑term solution for millions of people with the condition.
summary: Patients who took the daily pill baxdrostat for six to 12 months saw their blood pressure improve and the drug reversed a common cause of hypertension. The improvements persisted for up to two years after stopping the medication, with some patients no longer needing any hypertension drugs.
author: Guardian Science

title: Bininj rock shelter in Kakadu shows Namarrkon wielding lightning
content:
In a rock shelter in Kakadu National Park, the Bininj people have carved an image of Namarrkon, one of their most important creation ancestors. The carving shows Namarrkon’s flesh bleached away to reveal bone, stone axes fixed to his head, elbows, and knees, and a great band of lightning that extends from his ankles, over his head, and beyond.

Namarrkon’s journey from the coast to the Arnhem Land escarpment is believed to have shaped the surrounding landscape. In the great storms that sweep across the region during the wet season, the Bininj attribute the splitting of clouds, the thunder, the lightning, and the release of life‑giving rain to Namarrkon’s stone axes.

The depiction underscores the Bininj belief that Namarrkon’s power over thunder and lightning is integral to the creation and sustenance of their environment.
summary: Humans have always been awed by the power and beauty of lightning. How does the experience and understanding of it change in a warming world?
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA Calls for New Generation of Astronauts to Live and Work on the Moon
content:
NASA has announced a call for a new generation of astronauts who could live and work on the moon. Applications are open until 3 December as part of the latest expansion of the Artemis program.  

The agency says successful candidates will help “shape humanity’s future in space” by building a lunar base and preparing for the first crewed missions to Mars.
summary: NASA has opened applications for a new generation of astronauts to live and work on the moon, with the deadline on 3 December. Successful candidates will help shape humanity's future in space as the agency builds a lunar base and prepares for the first crewed missions to Mars.
author: Guardian Science

title: APOD features major fireball meteor captured over Italy on Nov 8 2026
content:
The Astronomy Picture of the Day for November 8, 2026 features a photograph taken on 14 November 2017 from a mountain pass in the Dolomite Alps of Italy. The image shows snowy, rugged peaks above the village of La Villa, Alta Badia, with the twilight sky rendered in soft pinkish hues. The constellation Ursa Major, including the Big Dipper asterism, is visible on the northern horizon.

During the camera’s exposure a bright fireball meteor crossed the sky from east to west, flashing above the village lights. The meteor was captured serendipitously in the same frame as the landscape. The event was reported widely across European skies, making it one of the most reported fireball occurrences recorded by the American Meteor Society and the International Meteor Organization.

Analysis of the meteor’s measured track over Germany indicates a trajectory consistent with an origin near the active radiant of the Northern Taurid meteor shower, which is associated with dust from Encke’s comet. The APOD entry credits the photograph to Ollie Taylor and lists Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, and Keighley Rockcliffe as authors and editors. The service is provided by ASD at NASA/GSFC, NASA Science Activation, and Michigan Tech.
summary: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 8 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.
author: NASA News

title: NASA launches $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge for U.S. schools
content:
NASA announced the opening of its $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge on Sunday during a MAX POWER event at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Florida. The competition, launched as part of a Golden Age of Science, invites student teams from U.S. high schools and post-secondary schools to submit designs for the Moon Base. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that the agency is seeking students who can think creatively, work as a team, and address real problems connected to NASA’s future on the Moon, emphasizing that curiosity and the willingness to tackle hard problems are essential qualities for building what comes next.

The Moon Base is being developed in the lunar South Pole region, where astronauts will live, work, and explore. A permanent human presence on the Moon is described as paving the way for future crewed missions to Mars and requiring talent from various industries and backgrounds. Carlos García-Galán, manager of the Moon Base Program, noted that the agency wants to leverage ingenuity and innovation to consider every need for explorers living and working on the lunar surface. He expressed anticipation for the fresh perspectives and bold ideas that students will bring to the project, stating that the Moon Base is ultimately for the next generation who will experience a world where humans remain on the Moon.

The multiphase challenge supports NASA’s commitment to cultivating the technical skills of tomorrow’s aerospace workforce. Student teams are tasked with designing innovative solutions across six specific categories: power generation and storage, construction, life-support systems, surface mobility, communications networks, and astronaut safety. The challenge provides participants with an opportunity to develop skills necessary for careers in the space industry while helping to advance new concepts for Moon Base technologies.

Participants must register for the challenge through the NASA STEM Gateway, with registration open until January 25, 2027. The challenge addresses authentic environmental and mission design parameters for life and operations on the lunar surface. Deliverables reflect industry skills such as trade studies, concept proposals, and stakeholder briefings, allowing participants across technical, vocational, and various academic tracks to build career-relevant skills without requiring prior specialized engineering or technical experience.

Elaine Ho, associate administrator for the Office of STEM Engagement at NASA Headquarters, described students as the next generation of explorers and innovators whose unique perspectives are key to envisioning a future away from Earth. The Office of STEM Engagement designed the challenge in collaboration with the Moon Base Program. The Institute of Competition Sciences administers the challenge through a contract with the NASA Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation within the agency’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. Complete competition details, eligibility requirements, and official rules are available at moonbasechallenge.org.
summary: Artist’s concept depicting astronauts, habitats, rovers, power systems, and cargo operations supporting sustained human activities at the Moon Base near the lunar South Pole. Credit: NASA On Sunday, NASA announced the opening of its $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge during a MAX POWER event at Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Florida.
author: NASA News

title: Apple’s 14‑inch MacBook Pro M6 announced as M5 model goes on sale
content: Apple announced an updated 14‑inch MacBook Pro equipped with the latest M6 chip. Meanwhile, the earlier M5 model is currently on sale, leading some to question whether the newer M6 version justifies an upgrade. The availability of the discounted M5 has sparked discussion about its value relative to the freshly announced M6‑powered device.
summary: Apple announced an updated 14‑inch MacBook Pro with the latest M6 chip. The M5 model is on sale, prompting doubt about whether the M6 upgrade is worthwhile.
author: Wired

title: NYT Cooking launches beta AI recipe modifier for ingredient swaps
content: The New York Times has introduced a beta AI‑powered “recipe modifier” in its Cooking app. The feature lets users swap ingredients or adjust recipes to meet their preferences, and, according to the report, it generally performs well.
summary: The New York Times has added a beta feature to its Cooking app that helps readers swap ingredients or adjust recipes to suit their needs. The AI‑powered recipe modifier mostly hits the mark.
author: Wired

title: NYT Cooking app's AI assistant rescues chicken dinner, nearly spoils cake
content: The NYT Cooking app now has a built in AI assistant. | Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge Around 7PM each weeknight, I find myself standing in front of the fridge, trying to decide on something for dinner that won't make my husband complain, "Chicken again?" Yes, I should meal plan more, but I don't, so this is where I'm at. A nightly battle in which the chicken usually wins. Recently, my best weapon in this fight has been AI. Between Alexa Plus in the Echo smart display on my kitchen counter, the Samsung Food app on my fridge, and even an AI-powered cooking robot, AI has become my go-to sous chef - albeit one I need to keep a close eye on. It's helped me swap ingredients, generate ideas, fix things when I mess up, and yes, even …
summary: The NYT Cooking app now includes a built‑in AI assistant. The author says the assistant helped save a weeknight chicken meal but almost ruined a cake.
author: The Verge

title: Costco members get $5 off Zelda Ocarina of Time remake
content: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake showcases plenty of modern effects. | Image: Nintendo While some retailers were offering preorder discounts on the remastered Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time, it’s not too late to save if you missed out. Costco members can currently get $5 off the digital version online, bringing the price down to $54.99. Considering an annual Costco membership runs $65, that discount almost offsets one month of your plan — a prime example of “gamer math.” The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time Where to Buy: $59.99 $54.99 at Costco (digital) My colleague Andrew Webster recently shared his thoughts on Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive, noting how impressed he was with how much impact a few modern quality-of-life changes had on what is otherwise a classic experience. The updated graphics are as thoughtful as they are beautiful, pairing realistic scenery with puppet-like characters. Perhaps, more importantly, Link can now jump anytime he likes, rather than being limited to specific ledges.
summary: Costco members can get $5 off the digital version of the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, lowering the price to $54.99. The discount is offered online and nearly offsets the cost of one month of the $65 annual Costco membership.
author: The Verge

title: UV-Tracking Necklace Gem Alerts Wearer to High Sun Exposure During LA Heat
content:
During a relative’s outdoor party in August, temperatures in Los Angeles reached the 90s. The writer sat beneath a patio umbrella with a powerful fan, assuming protection from the heat. After about thirty minutes, the writer experienced exhaustion, dizziness, nausea, and general illness—symptoms consistent with heat exhaustion.

At the same time, a notification from an app linked to a $249 (later $149) UV‑tracking necklace called Gem, manufactured by The90, alerted the wearer that UV exposure had risen significantly. The alert coincided with the onset of the writer’s heat‑related symptoms.
summary: The author wore a Gem UV‑tracking necklace from The90, priced at $249 ($149 at time of publication), while attending a relative’s outdoor party in Los Angeles in August. The necklace’s app notified the author that UV exposure had risen sharply as they experienced heat‑exhaustion symptoms.
author: The Verge

title: Media industry’s video pivot continues unabated, says The Stepback
content: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the pressures of creating content for the internet, follow Mia Sato. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started Almost exactly a decade ago, the media industry was in the middle of a video revolution - or so it thought. In the mid-2010s, publications poured money into burgeoning social media video efforts, chasing the promise of reaching larger audiences and opening new lines of revenue. Print publications and digital news outlets alike hired teams, pumped out c …
summary: About a decade ago the media industry launched a video revolution, investing in social‑media video and hiring dedicated teams. The article notes that the shift to video 2.0 shows no sign of slowing.
author: The Verge

title: Apple iOS 27.3 beta hints at chatbot support for HomeView
content:
Code in the iOS 27.3 beta includes a flag for a “Conversational Apps” category, suggesting Apple may enable chatbot support on its HomeView smart‑home hub. The beta does not specify which apps could use the category, but the presence of the flag implies that AI chatbots such as ChatGPT or Claude could be added.

The same beta also introduces bidirectional audio routing and session‑management features, which a source identified as pdfu on X described as “still not fully wired up.” Additionally, Apple has added anti‑spoofing protection that will prompt users to authenticate with an iPhone after three failed attempts and will enforce a lockout mechanism.
summary: Code in the iOS 27.3 beta adds a “Conversational Apps” flag, suggesting Apple may enable AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude on its HomeView hub. The beta also introduces bidirectional audio routing, session management and anti‑spoofing that locks out after three failed authentication attempts.
author: The Verge

title: Apple’s M5 MacBook Air hits lowest price since July
content:
Apple’s M5‑powered 13‑inch MacBook Air is now listed at $1,099.99, the lowest price it has reached since July. The discount represents a $200 reduction and is the second time the model has been offered at this level after the company’s summer price increases. The base configuration includes the M5 processor, 16 GB of RAM and a 512 GB SSD, and it is being sold at the reduced price by Amazon, Best Buy and B&H Photo in all color options.

When the 13‑inch Air launched in May, it typically sold for roughly $950 to $1,000, but price cuts have been uncommon since July, making the current offer notable. A larger 15‑inch MacBook Air, which adds a six‑speaker array and two extra GPU cores, is also discounted by $200 and is priced at $1,299.99 for the same 16 GB RAM/512 GB SSD configuration. The 15‑inch model is likewise available from Amazon, Best Buy and B&H Photo in most colors.

The article notes that, despite being more expensive than the newer MacBook Neo, the Air provides “better value” through double the RAM, a faster CPU with more cores, twice the storage, improved speakers, a backlit keyboard and a larger, higher‑resolution screen. Readers are directed to earlier reviews of the MacBook Neo and the M5 MacBook Air for additional context.
summary: A top-down view of the 15-inch MacBook Air, which features Apple’s M5 processor. | Photo: Antonio G.
author: The Verge

title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders sue AI music firm Suno over voice cloning
content:
Sun​o, an AI music company, is being sued in two separate actions. One suit is brought by a group of rights holders of Elvis Presley’s music, and the other by the publisher of several of Eminem’s major records. Both parties allege that Sun​o illegally generates music and lyrics that imitate the respective artists.

In the Presley case, the plaintiffs’ lawyers contend that Sun​o has violated Tennessee’s Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security (ELVIS) Act, which prohibits an AI firm from cloning a singer’s voice. They further argue that “Suno has mechanically encoded itself with artists’ identities, hard‑work, creativity, and time, and harnessed them all for …”. The lawsuits claim the company’s technology infringes on the artists’ protected rights.
summary: Suno is facing yet another pair of lawsuits. A group of rights holders of Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of some of Eminem's biggest records are suing the AI music company, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists.
author: The Verge

title: British soldier court-martialed after refusing to remove SIM card, blackmailed
content:
An Estonian newspaper reported that British soldier Daniel Barton‑Kennedy ignored a direct order to remove the SIM card from his cellphone before being deployed to a location in Estonia about 90 miles west of the Russian border. After refusing the operational‑security measure, his phone was hacked, nude photographs were stolen and used to blackmail him.

Barton‑Kennedy was subsequently court‑martialed for disobeying a lawful command, pleaded guilty, was reduced in rank and sentenced to ten months’ detention.
summary: British soldier court-martialed after refusing to remove SIM card, blackmailed.
author: Ars Technica

title: Scientists study Great Zimbabwe iron furnaces to trace Bantu expansion impact
content:
Scientists continue to investigate how the Bantu expansion reshaped Africa, seeking evidence of the cultural and technological changes it brought. One focus of current research is the iron‑working expertise demonstrated by the ancient inhabitants of Great Zimbabwe, the capital of a prosperous southern‑African kingdom that flourished from roughly 1000 to 1700 AD.

Archaeologists have identified clusters of iron‑smelting furnaces near the stone ruins of Great Zimbabwe, now visible as mounds of rubble. At the nearby village of Mashava, about 25 miles northwest, fragments of furnace interiors retain the fingerprints of the workers who once smoothed the clay. Some furnaces measured nearly an adult’s arm span across and featured thick walls capable of containing temperatures above 2,100 °F, sufficient to melt iron ore. Unlike many contemporary furnaces that required manual bellows, these structures drew air in and expelled it through a chimney, eliminating the need for human labor and facilitating the production of tools such as hoes, axes and arrowheads.
summary: Scientists are still tracing how the Bantu expansion changed Africa. The iron‑smelting furnaces at Great Zimbabwe, a capital from 1000‑1700 AD, were large self‑ventilating structures that produced iron for hoes, axes and arrowheads without using bellows.
author: Ars Technica

title: Physicists use electrical noise to probe cuprate pseudogap
content: Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don't agree on why. In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate. The missing electrons Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there's these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said. Read full article Comments
summary: Physicists Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University measured the faint electrical crackle from current flowing into a cuprate to study its pseudogap. Their recent Science study reports that the pseudogap involves missing electrons above the superconducting temperature, offering new clues to high‑temperature superconductivity.
author: Ars Technica

title: Companies launch kid-focused phones as parents seek safer alternatives
content: Parents are seeking alternatives to unrestricted smartphones for their children. In response, a growing number of companies are developing phones designed specifically for kids, offering options that range from feature‑limited mobile devices to minimalist home phones.
summary: Parents are looking for alternatives to unrestricted smartphones. A growing number of companies are building phones designed specifically for kids, from feature‑limited mobile devices to minimalist home phones.
author: TechCrunch

title: Leaked docs reveal Cisco expanded Israeli military contracts amid Gaza war
content:
Leaked documents reveal that Cisco intensified its dealings with Israel’s military intelligence during the Gaza war, despite internal protests by workers over the company’s involvement. The tech conglomerate “leaped to shore up” its relationship with the Israeli agencies even as the firm faced criticism from its own staff.

A year into the conflict, Israel’s military intelligence networks experienced prolonged outages, multi‑hour system crashes and failed debugging mechanisms. These persistent technical problems eroded the confidence of the intelligence agencies in Cisco, one of their primary network providers.
summary: Leaked documents show Cisco increased its deals with Israel’s military intelligence during the Gaza war. The company sought to shore up the relationship despite worker protests and repeated network outages that had eroded Israeli confidence in its services.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Trump administration plans four underwater datacenters off Maine and Alaska
content:
Tech companies are increasingly interested in underwater data‑center concepts, citing reduced community opposition and lower utility costs as key advantages. Elon Musk has long promoted space‑based data‑centers, but recent reports indicate a shift toward aquatic sites.

Two underwater data‑center facilities already operate off the coast of China. Meanwhile, the Trump administration is reportedly exploring plans for four proposed underwater, sealed‑pod data‑centers to be built off the shores of Maine and Alaska. The proposal reflects a growing trend to harness the natural cooling and isolation benefits of submerged environments for large‑scale computing.
summary: The Trump administration is considering building four sealed‑pod underwater datacenters off the coasts of Maine and Alaska. Two underwater datacenters already operate off China’s coast, and a Great Lakes nonprofit is preparing its own underwater facility.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Lanarkshire AI datacentre will rely entirely on National Grid, not renewable power
content: DataVita has revised plan for Chapelhall development to be wholly powered by 1GW of renewable energy A datacentre company that said it would power a massive AI development near Glasgow with renewable energy has admitted that the scheme will be entirely served by the National Grid. DataVita, a key plank of the UK’s AI strategy, had promised that the Lanarkshire project would draw 1GW – the equivalent output of a small nuclear reactor, or Britain’s largest windfarm – from green sources. But when the Guardian raised questions about the pledge, it said the arrangement was “subject to final commercial agreements, planning, grid and consenting processes”.
summary: DataVita said the Lanarkshire AI datacentre will be wholly served by the National Grid. The company had earlier pledged the Chapelhall project would draw 1 GW of renewable energy, but said the arrangement is subject to final commercial, planning, grid and consenting processes.
author: Guardian Technology

title: FAA launches first U.S. digital air traffic control towers in Florida and Alaska
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration announced that the United States’ first digital air‑traffic‑control towers are now operational. The new systems, which provide a 360‑degree view of airport operations, have been installed at Bartow Executive Airport (KBOW) in Florida and Kenai Municipal Airport (PAEN) in Alaska.  

The FAA noted that five additional regional airports are slated to receive the same technology, as the current administration moves forward with upgrades to the nation’s aging aviation infrastructure, despite some concerns that have been raised about the technology.
summary: The Federal Aviation Administration announced that digital air traffic control towers are now operational at Bartow executive airport (KBOW) in Florida and Kenai municipal airport (PAEN) in Alaska. Five additional regional airports are slated to receive the technology next.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Thailand pauses 49 datacentre projects as power, water constraints curb growth
content:
The rapid expansion of datacentre capacity in south‑east Asia has stalled. In early 2026 Thailand’s datacentre sector appeared to be booming, with the Board of Investment approving projects from TikTok, a UAE‑based Skyline datacentre and Singapore’s Bridge Datacentres, amounting to a planned $27 billion in investment.

By September 2026 the momentum slowed as Thailand paused construction on 49 projects and deferred approval decisions on 117 more, citing power and water constraints and concerns over insufficient regulatory and monitoring details. The slowdown is not isolated. In Indonesia, the governor of West Java halted construction on a datacentre because permits were lacking and the environmental assessment process was incomplete. These actions reflect growing scrutiny of datacentre development in the region.
summary: Thailand halted construction on 49 datacentre projects and paused approval of 117 projects in September 2026 due to power, water constraints and regulatory concerns. In West Java, Indonesia, the provincial governor stopped a datacentre build because of missing permits and an incomplete environmental assessment.
author: Guardian Technology

title: 78‑year‑old Philadelphia professor Carolyn Marvin blocks food‑delivery robots
content: Semi-retired professor Carolyn Marvin became a local celebrity facing down Philadelphia’s growing robot delivery army: ‘It’s my first amendment right to protest’ “One of you needs to be on the lookout for cops, while I block the robot, OK?” It is a crisp fall morning in Philadelphia. Tucked away in a dingy alley, opposite a garage called Patriot Parking, 78-year-old Carolyn Marvin is laying out some ground rules for a robot-disrupting expedition. Once a suitable target is identified, we will follow it to a busy sidewalk and Marvin will stand in front of the robot, blocking its way. The photographer and I will take turns ensuring we’re not all carted off by the police.
summary: Semi‑retired professor Carolyn Marvin, a 78‑year‑old local celebrity in Philadelphia, confronts the city’s robot food‑delivery fleet by standing in front of the machines. She says it is her First Amendment right to protest and works with a photographer to avoid police intervention.
author: Guardian Technology

title: UK public bodies face surge of AI‑generated complaints, says Labour MP caseworker
content:
UK public bodies—including MPs, local authorities, lawyers and schools—are reporting a surge of complaints, requests and legal challenges that appear to be generated by artificial‑intelligence chatbots. Hollie Wickens, a senior caseworker in a Labour MP’s office, says the volume began as a “trickle in 2024” and has grown into an “onslaught.”  

Wickens notes that about half of the emails her office receives are some form of AI‑produced correspondence, making the material “much more complex and time‑consuming to read and deal with” despite her decade of experience. She describes the workload as “definitely more taxing.”
summary: MPs, local authorities, lawyers, schools and other public bodies are receiving a flood of AI‑generated grievances, requests and legal challenges. Senior caseworker Hollie Wickens of a Labour MP’s office says about half of the emails they receive are AI‑generated, making the correspondence more complex and time‑consuming to read and handle.
author: Guardian Technology

title: London wholesaler spots 150°C defrost lights on two fridges amid rising cyber‑attack fears
content:
The piece asks whether recent incidents – hot fridges, a fake nuclear alert and a $6 billion heist – signal the start of a broader hacking epidemic. It notes that, as AI highlights weaknesses in IT systems and geopolitics unfolds on the cyber front, some experts warn that such events could become routine.

In a concrete example, Alex Pearce was conducting his morning rounds at a fruit and vegetable wholesale business in London when he saw the defrost light on refrigeration unit 2 illuminated and the panel reading 150 °C; unit 4 showed the same readings.
summary: Alex Pearce observed the defrost lights on refrigeration units 2 and 4 at his London fruit and vegetable wholesale business were on, with panel readings of 150 °C. Experts say recent cyber incidents such as fake nuclear alerts and a $6 bn heist suggest a growing hacking threat.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Egypt announces new Mediterranean gas field with 200 bcf estimate
content: Egypt announced the discovery of a new Mediterranean gas field with an estimated reserve of 200 billion cubic feet. The Ministry of Petroleum said the positive outcome reflects higher investment and exploration activity, an improved investment climate, and progress in settling overdue payments to foreign energy‑sector companies.
summary: Egypt announced the discovery of a new Mediterranean gas field estimated at 200 billion cubic feet. The Ministry of Petroleum said the positive results stem from higher investment and exploration activity, a better investment climate, and progress in settling overdue payments to foreign companies in the energy sector.
author: Euronews

title: Egypt reopens Tripoli embassy after 12 years, objects to Turkey-Libya maritime deal
content: Egypt has reopened its embassy in Tripoli after a 12‑year closure as it seeks closer ties with Libya’s western government, shifting from its previous support for the eastern rival. In Tripoli, officials discussed energy projects and voiced Egypt’s objections to Libya’s maritime agreement with Turkey.
summary: Egypt is seeking closer ties with Libya’s western government after years of backing its eastern rival. Talks in Tripoli covered energy projects and Egypt’s objections to Libya’s maritime deal with Turkey.
author: Euronews

title: Four dead, 88 injured in train collision 52 km south of Cairo
content: At least four people were killed and 88 injured when two trains collided about 52 kilometres south of Cairo, with one train striking the rear of the other and causing a derailment. Egyptian President Abdelfatah al‑Sisi has ordered an investigation to determine the causes and responsibility.
summary: At least four people were killed and 88 were injured when one train hit the rear of another about 52 kilometres south of Cairo, causing a derailment. President Abdelfatah al‑Sisi ordered an investigation to determine the causes and responsibility.
author: Euronews

title: Hackers claim Rosstat data shows 393,000‑450,000 Russian deaths in Ukraine war
content: Hacker groups Cyberpartisans BY and Silent Crow say they breached Russia’s statistical agency Rosstat and compiled figures on Russian casualties since the invasion of Ukraine. Their analysis puts the death toll between 393,000 and 450,000 people.
summary: Hacker groups Cyberpartisans BY and Silent Crow say they hacked Rosstat and counted Russian losses since the invasion of Ukraine. They estimate the number of Russian deaths at between 393,000 and 450,000.
author: Euronews

title: Erdoğan attends Azerbaijan's sixth Victory Day ceremony in Karabakh with Aliyev
content: Azerbaijan celebrated on Sunday its sixth Victory Day, marking the end of the Karabakh war. Turkey's Erdoğan joined the commemorations to underscore the strength of bilateral ties despite recent differences, with Aliyev declaring that "this unity will last forever".
summary: Azerbaijan celebrated its sixth Victory Day on Sunday, marking the end of the Karabakh war. Turkey's Erdoğan attended the commemorations with Aliyev, who said the unity will last forever.
author: Euronews

title: French sailor Tom Laperche wins Route du Rhum, sets new record
content: French sailor Tom Laperche, 29, won the Route du Rhum, crossing the finish line in Guadeloupe on his first attempt. His time set a new record for the transatlantic yacht race, beating the 2022 record by about six hours.
summary: Tom Laperche, a 29‑year‑old French sailor, won the Route du Rhum by finishing in Guadeloupe on his first attempt. He beat the previous 2022 record by around six hours.
author: France 24

title: Poland launches terror probe after six killed in Krakow shooting
content: Poland on Sunday launched a terror probe into the mass shooting in Krakow the day before, in which six people were killed and many more were injured. Authorities have said that the 24-year-old suspect, who used a semi-automatic rifle in his killing spree, was “fascinated by far-right ideologies”. He is currently in critical condition in hospital. FRANCE 24 journalist Adrien Sariat reports from Poland.
summary: Poland opened a terror investigation into a mass shooting in Krakow that left six people dead and many injured. Authorities said the 24‑year‑old suspect, who used a semi‑automatic rifle and is fascinated by far‑right ideologies, is in critical condition in hospital.
author: France 24

title: US voters reject most AI data centre measures in midterm elections
content:
In Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections, voters considered more than 40 local measures concerning AI data‑centre projects and rejected them in every case except one. The outcomes reflect a broad rejection of new data‑centre construction at the ballot box.

The defeats come as Democrats are set to control Congress in January, while newly elected governors in Texas and Georgia have announced calls for moratoriums on AI data‑centre development, marking a significant political challenge for the industry’s expansion.
summary: In Tuesday’s US midterm elections, voters rejected all but one of more than 40 local measures on AI data centres. Democrats took control of Congress in January and the new governors of Texas and Georgia have called for moratoriums, creating a tough political test for the AI building boom.
author: France 24

title: US midterm 'Blue Wave' wins, French student protests, Dakar Youth Olympics highlighted
content: FRANCE 24 has compiled a visual recap of the week, featuring images of the Democratic Party’s large victories in the United States midterm elections, the ongoing student‑led protests across France, and the inaugural Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, marking the first Olympic sports event held on African soil.
summary: The Democratic Party secured big wins in the US midterm elections. France saw ongoing student-led protests and Dakar hosted the first Olympic sports event on African soil.
author: France 24

title: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Ben Shelton to claim first Paris Masters title
content: Spanish tennis star Carlos Alcaraz defeated American Ben Shelton to claim his first Paris Masters title, avenging a September US Open loss to Shelton. The victory moved Alcaraz ahead of his rival on Sunday, while it marked Shelton’s first defeat in a Masters final.
summary: Spanish tennis star Carlos Alcaraz beat American player Ben Shelton to win the Paris Masters, his first title at the event. The win avenged Alcaraz's September US Open loss and was Shelton's first defeat in a Masters final.
author: France 24

title: Israel's opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot tasked with forming new government
content:
Israel’s opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been formally tasked with forming the country’s next government after President Isaac Herzog announced the mandate. Eisenkot has up to six weeks to negotiate with potential coalition partners and secure a parliamentary majority.

The report notes that an alliance with Arab Israeli parties would be the mathematically simplest path to a majority, though it is described as politically sensitive. Eisenkot’s negotiations aim to build a coalition capable of replacing Benjamin Netanyahu, according to Noga Tarnopolsky reporting from Jerusalem.
summary: Gadi Eisenkot has been officially assigned by President Isaac Herzog to build Israel's next government. He has up to six weeks to negotiate coalition partners, with an Arab Israeli party alliance seen as mathematically easiest but politically sensitive, as he aims to replace Benjamin Netanyahu.
author: France 24

title: Russian airstrikes cut power for hundreds of thousands in Ukraine
content: Hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians lost electricity on Sunday after Russian airstrikes hit the country’s energy infrastructure. The attacks, which Moscow has intensified as winter approaches, have left residents in Kyiv and other regions coping with power cuts amid falling temperatures, according to reporter Clemence Waller.
summary: Hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians were left without electricity on Sunday after Russian airstrikes hit the country's energy infrastructure. The attacks, which Moscow has intensified as winter approaches, left residents in Kyiv and other areas coping with power cuts as temperatures drop.
author: France 24

title: Democrats consider next moves after Republicans lose congressional majority
content: Donald Trump’s Republican Party has lost its majority in both the House and the Senate, giving Democrats a congressional win in the midterms. While the president retains significant authority, Democratic leaders have not yet reached consensus on how to deploy their newfound power.
summary: Donald Trump's Republican party has lost its majority in both chambers of the US Congress. The president still has a lot of power — and the Democrats have yet to agree on how best to use theirs.
author: DW World

title: Reza Pahlavi receives Freedom Prize in Frankfurt amid 18,000‑person rally
content: Reza Pahlavi, the son of Iran’s deposed monarch, was presented with a “Freedom Prize” in Frankfurt before a crowd of about 18,000 supporters. Some opposition factions have criticized him for not distancing himself from his father’s rule.
summary: Reza Pahlavi, son of Iran’s former monarch, was awarded a Freedom Prize in Frankfurt before a crowd of about 18,000 supporters. Some opposition factions have criticized him for not distancing himself from his father’s rule.
author: DW World

title: Publishers claim AI chatbots use their reporting, reducing traffic and revenue
content: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?
summary: Publishers claim AI chatbots use their reporting, reducing traffic and revenue.
author: DW World

title: Armenian civil society warns EU of selective prosecution of opposition
content: Armenian civil society has warned that opposition figures are facing selective justice, while the European Union has so far avoided harsh criticism of the situation. Observers question whether the EU’s pragmatic stance could lead to a repeat of earlier mistakes in its relations with Armenia.
summary: Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, prompting concerns that the EU's pragmatic stance could repeat past mistakes.
author: DW World

title: President Isaac Herzog appoints Gadi Eisenkot to form Israeli government
content: President Isaac Herzog has selected former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who leads an anti‑Netanyahu alliance, to make the first attempt at forming a government. Officials anticipate that coalition negotiations will be difficult.
summary: President Isaac Herzog has picked former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of an anti‑Netanyahu alliance, to try forming a government. Coalition talks are expected to be tricky.
author: DW World

title: Bundibugyo Ebola strain still has no vaccine, new research offers hope
content: Ebola has been known for decades, yet there is still no vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain driving the current outbreak. New research, however, is reported to raise hopes of achieving protection against the various types of Ebola.
summary: Ebola has been known about for decades, but there is still no vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus causing the current outbreak. New research raises hopes of protection against the various types of Ebola.
author: DW World

title: ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa municipal election
content: The African National Congress, the party of late Nobel Prize winner Nelson Mandela, recorded its worst‑ever result in South Africa’s municipal election. Voters attributed the outcome to the ANC’s handling of water and electricity shortages.
summary: The African National Congress slumped to its worst-ever result in South Africa's municipal election. Voters blamed the ANC for water and electricity shortages.
author: DW World

title: COP31 host says summit must deliver tangible climate progress as 190 nations meet
content: High-stakes talks involving 190 countries begin on Monday as world grapples with El Niño supercharged by fossil fuels The Cop31 summit must produce progress, “a tangible outcome... That people can see is real”, its host has said as scores of world leaders and representatives of close to 190 countries gather in Turkey for the UN climate talks. The high-stakes meeting begins on Monday, as countries around the world grapple with the strongest El Niño weather system on record, supercharged by fossil fuels, which is set to take hundreds of thousands of lives and cause damage costing trillions of dollars.
summary: COP31 host says summit must deliver tangible climate progress as 190 nations meet.
author: Guardian World

title: IFPI warns Albanese government weakening AI copyright law endangers creativity
content: Exclusive: Head of IFPI says allowing AI companies access to online content would be a ‘huge mistake’ and damage Australia’s reputation Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Australia weakening copyright protections for AI companies would be “ridiculous and dangerous”, the global peak body for the music recording industry has warned as it watches with concern how the Albanese government responds to big tech’s demands. While local creatives have raised constitutional issues and threatened political backlash, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), representing recording industry bodies worldwide, said its members were worried about Australia potentially agreeing to demands other nations had rejected.
summary: IFPI warns Albanese government weakening AI copyright law endangers creativity.
author: Guardian World

title: NZ election 2026 results too close to call as National leads but coalition uncertain
content: National party will be largest in parliament but ultimate shape of next government won’t be settled for some time New Zealand could be facing a weeks-long wait to know the shape of its next government, after its nail-biting election failed to hand a decisive victory to either the incumbent rightwing coalition or opposition left bloc. On preliminary results, the centre-right National party, led by the prime minister, Christopher Luxon, managed to secure enough seats to govern alongside its traditional coalition partners, the libertarian Act and populist New Zealand First parties.
summary: NZ election 2026 results too close to call as National leads but coalition uncertain.
author: Guardian World

title: Thailand to deport two Uyghurs to China, activists say they face slavery
content:
Activists warn that Bangkok may yield to Beijing’s pressure, even as reports of torture and other human‑rights abuses against the predominantly Muslim Uyghur minority circulate.

The potential deportation of two more Uyghurs would place their lives in grave danger, activists say. One of the men said he would be “like a slave” if sent back. Last year, Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghur men to China despite pleas from the men themselves and the UN. The US and Canada had offered to resettle them, but Bangkok appeared intent on avoiding upsetting Beijing. The UN reports the returnees’ whereabouts remain unknown.
summary: Thailand to deport two Uyghurs to China, activists say they face slavery.
author: Guardian World

title: Pope Leo XIV visits Argentine disability home as President Milei cuts funding
content: President has opposing views on many issues, and once called Leo’s predecessor the ‘representative of the Evil One’ Trees are being planted in the garden. The brightly coloured buildings are getting another coat of paint. The choir rehearses. Hundreds of other residents, several of them using wheelchairs, practise their positions outside the sanctuary. Excitement is in the air, because on Monday 9 November, the Cottolengo Don Orione – a Catholic-run home for disabled people – will be the first stop on Pope Leo XIV’s first full day of his trip to Argentina. But the pope’s visit to Claypole, about 26km from Buenos Aires, does not come at an especially happy time for the home, which counts about 400 residents with disabilities. Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has made wide-ranging cuts to disability funding.
summary: Pope Leo XIV will begin his first full day in Argentina on Monday 9 November with a visit to the Cottolengo Don Orione home for disabled people in Claypole, about 26 km from Buenos Aires. The home, which houses about 400 residents, is affected by wide‑range cuts to disability funding announced by President Javier Milei.
author: Guardian World

title: See My World festival in Manchester draws on African philosophies, held Nov 21
content:
The event “See My World” will showcase pan‑African thought through film, poetry and dance, drawing on momentum generated by local activists and creatives. Organisers say African philosophies—particularly reflections on how past lessons can influence the present and near future—have inspired a new approach to staging a film festival in Manchester.

“See My World” is a day‑long program dedicated to independent creators from the African diaspora in the north of England and is scheduled for 21 November at the Contact theatre.
summary: See My World highlights pan‑African thought through film, poetry and dance and draws inspiration from African philosophies. The day‑long event for independent creators from the African diaspora in northern England will be held at the Contact Theatre on 21 November.
author: Guardian World

title: Train collision in al‑Ayyat, Egypt kills at least seven, injures over 100
content:
A train collision in Egypt’s al‑Ayyat district, about 30 miles south of Cairo, killed at least seven people and injured more than 100, officials said. The accident occurred on Sunday when a train bound for the south‑western Fayoum province struck the rear of a train traveling toward the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.

President [Name not provided] ordered a prompt investigation into the derailment. The crash took place in Giza province’s al‑Ayyat district, roughly 30 miles from the capital.
summary: Seven people were killed and more than 100 injured when two trains collided in al‑Ayyat district, Giza province, about 30 miles south of Cairo. The president ordered a prompt investigation after a train bound for Fayoum province struck the rear of a train heading to Aswan.
author: Guardian World

title: Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis steps away from basketball for undisclosed health issue
content:
Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis announced on Friday that he is stepping away from basketball to prioritize his health. The 31‑year‑old posted the decision on his X account, stating that an undisclosed health issue prompted the move. Porziņģis did not provide further details about the nature of the problem.

He did not clarify whether he will resume playing, leaving the possibility of a return open after a long absence. The announcement was made via social media, and no additional information about the health matter or future plans has been released. The Warriors have not issued a statement.
summary: Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis, 31, announced on his X account on Friday that he is stepping away from basketball to prioritize his health. He did not disclose the nature of the health issue and did not confirm whether he will resume playing.
author: Guardian Sport

title: UKFPU prioritizes antisocial behavior by teenage ultras in non-league football
content: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous?
summary: The UK Football Policing Unit has declared antisocial behavior by teenage ultras its most important priority due to increasing disorder in non-league football. Communities fear that current trouble-making by groups like the "schooligans" will eventually become more dangerous.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Trump, Fifa president, and Australian redback spider study headline news
content: Trump Exposed Reactor Core Syndrome very much in play after Democrat landslide – and Fifa’s president may pay a price Oh baby, clamp me in your repulsive mouthparts. Sink your unusually large and venomous fangs into my abdomen. And yes, we are doing this in the White House cabinet rooms, out there in plain sight of the watching world, just a gleaming golden ball between us. But it’s fine. Probably. Now take a sip of those sweet, sweet tiny male arachnoid entrails. An exciting new study was published over the summer into the habits of the Australian redback spider. The research made headlines for its focus on reproductive behaviour, specifically the male’s urgent and very willing engagement in what is known as sexual cannibalism, AKA copulatory suicide.
summary: Trump is exposed after a Democrat landslide, and Fifa’s president may pay a price. A study on the Australian redback spider revealed male sexual cannibalism.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Man City loses last two after winning first seven; Leeds vs Spurs points low
content: ⚽ All the latest news before a busy day of football kicks off ⚽ Today’s fixtures | Latest tables | Mail us at matchday. Live An email. Krishnamoorthy v has been pondering today’s games. Hello David. Would Leeds be able to puncture the nascent baloon of Tottenham optimism (if ever there was a candidate for a perfect oxymoron, this would ace it) and can we expect City to lose its way in the forest? Leeds v Spurs: Leeds have picked up just five points in their last 13 Premier League matches against Tottenham. Nottingham Forest v Man City: Having become the 10th team in English top-flight history to win each of their first seven games in a campaign, Man City have now lost their last two. Only Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05 have won their first seven and then lost their next three.
summary: Leeds have earned only five points in their last 13 Premier League matches against Tottenham. Man City have won each of their first seven games in the campaign but have now lost their last two.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lampard frustrated after three big decisions cost Coventry in 3-1 loss to Everton
content: Frank Lampard, the head coach of Coventry City, voiced frustration after his team suffered a 3‑1 defeat to Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. He cited three “big decisions” that he felt went against his side.
summary: Frank Lampard, head coach of Coventry City, was frustrated after three "big decisions" went against his side. The decisions contributed to Coventry's 3-1 defeat by Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.
author: BBC Sport

title: James Trafford says missing out at Man City was 'horrendous', leaves for Leeds United
content: James Trafford says not playing for Manchester City last season was "horrendous" and left him with no choice but to leave the club and join Leeds United in the summer.
summary: James Trafford said that not playing for Manchester City last season was 'horrendous'. He said it left him with no choice but to leave the club and join Leeds United in the summer.
author: BBC Sport

title: Altrincham target Notts County as next FA Cup giant‑killer
content: Altrincham, a non‑league side known for their FA Cup upsets, are targeting Notts County as the next club to add to their tally of giant‑killer victories. If successful, the defeat would become the 18th scalp on the club’s list, reinforcing their reputation as English football’s ultimate giant‑killers.
summary: Altrincham, a non‑league club, are targeting Notts County as the 18th team on their FA Cup scalp list. The club hopes to revive its reputation as English football's ultimate giant‑killers.
author: BBC Sport

title: Giuliani says Vance could be a dangerous presidential prospect
content: Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani told viewers on Thursday that he sees “presidential potential” in Vice President Vance, but warned of “certain dangers” in Vance’s personality. Giuliani made the remarks during a livestream on his YouTube channel.
summary: Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani said he sees presidential potential in Vice President Vance during a livestream on his YouTube channel. He also warned that Vance has certain dangers in his personality.
author: The Hill

title: Democrat Sean McCann defeats Bill Huizenga in Michigan's 4th Congressional District
content:
Democrat Sean McCann has won Michigan’s 4th Congressional District, ousting longtime Rep. Bill Huizenga (R), according to Decision Desk HQ.

Huizenga has represented western Michigan in the House for more than a decade and easily won his last race in 2024, but the district has become more competitive in recent years.
summary: Democrat Sean McCann has won Michigan’s 4th Congressional District, ousting longtime Rep. Bill Huizenga (R). Huizenga has represented western Michigan in the House for more than a decade.
author: The Hill

title: Sen. Ron Johnson seeks to postpone Senate GOP leadership vote after losses
content: Sen. Ron Johnson (R-Wis.), a staunch Trump ally and chair of the Senate Budget Committee, has secured the five signatures required from GOP colleagues to request a meeting of the Senate Republican Conference. Johnson is seeking to delay the party’s leadership election, currently scheduled for next week, following significant losses.
summary: Sen. Ron Johnson (R-Wis.) obtained the five signatures he needs from GOP colleagues to request a meeting of the broader Senate Republican Conference to discuss postponing their leadership election, which is scheduled for next week.
author: The Hill

title: Houston Mayor John Whitmire to limit city cooperation with ICE after Democratic wins
content:
Houston Mayor John Whitmire (D) announced that the city will limit its cooperation with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers. The announcement came days after Democrats swept state‑level offices in the midterm elections.  

Whitmire’s executive order specifically applies to nonviolent criminals, who will be released with a citation. The mayor noted that the order addresses ICE cooperation only under the conditions outlined in the directive.
summary: Houston Mayor John Whitmire (D) said the city will limit cooperation with ICE officers. He said his executive order applies to nonviolent criminals, who will be released with a citation, and announced it just days after Democrats swept state‑level offices in the midterm elections.
author: The Hill

title: Former Gov. Tommy Thompson says Wisconsin is now a blue state
content: Former Wisconsin Gov. Tommy Thompson (R) declared the Badger State blue in a post-election interview Wednesday, pointing to recent statewide defeats for the GOP — including in its gubernatorial race. “Wisconsin is no longer a purple state,” Thompson told Wisconsin Public Radio. “We haven’t won a statewide race for a long time. Wisconsin is a…
summary: Former Wisconsin Governor Tommy Thompson, a Republican, said Wisconsin is no longer a purple state and is now a blue state in a post‑election interview. He pointed to recent GOP defeats in statewide races, including the gubernatorial contest, noting the party has not won a statewide race for a long time.
author: The Hill

title: Sen. Thom Tillis calls Stephen Miller the worst possible chief of staff pick
content: Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N. C.) blasted President Trump’s Friday decision to replace outgoing White House chief of staff Susie Wiles with top adviser Stephen Miller, saying the president “needs to rethink” his decision. “I’ve criticized a lot of the president’s advisors for bad advice that I think … created some of the environment on Tuesday, but…
summary: Sen. Thom Tillis calls Stephen Miller the worst possible chief of staff pick.
author: The Hill

title: Study finds childcare's effect on child napping reverses as kids age
content:
A well‑napped child is often described as cheerful and happy. In a society where both parents typically work, most children attend childcare during their first five years—a period that coincides with the shift from regular daytime naps to sleeping through the night.

A recent study published in Sleep Medicine examined whether attending childcare alters the number of naps a child takes in a day compared with days spent at home. The research also explored how this relationship changes as children age.
summary: A well-napped child is a cheerful and happy child. In a world where both parents have to work, most children spend their first five years attending childcare, right around the time they transition from regular daytime naps to sleeping through the night.
author: Medical Xpress

title: SCAI releases 2026 SHOCK Classification update to refine cardiogenic shock assessment
content: The Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions released the 2026 SCAI SHOCK Classification Expert Consensus Update, refining guidance for clinicians to assess cardiogenic shock, prioritize inadequate organ perfusion, evaluate shock severity over time, and determine if treatment restores adequate circulation.
summary: The Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions (SCAI) issued the 2026 SCAI SHOCK Classification Expert Consensus Update. The update provides refined guidance for clinicians to prioritize and recognize inadequate organ perfusion, assess shock severity over time, and determine if treatment is restoring adequate circulation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: King's College London researchers create better method to detect preeclampsia in EHRs
content: Researchers at King’s College London have developed a more precise method for identifying preeclampsia within electronic health records. The new approach enables the capture of cases and related adverse outcomes that existing methods may overlook.
summary: Researchers at King's College London have developed a more effective method for identifying preeclampsia from electronic health records. The method captures cases and associated adverse outcomes that existing methods may miss.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Metformin may cut long COVID or death risk by 53% if given early
content: Metformin may lower the risk of long COVID or death by 53 % when prescribed early, according to a recent study. Long COVID—new‑onset symptoms or worsening health conditions after SARS‑CoV‑2 infection—can reduce quality of life, and preventing it would provide relief for those concerned about lasting effects.
summary: Metformin may lower the risk of long COVID or death by 53% when prescribed early. Long COVID refers to new symptoms or worsening health conditions after SARS‑CoV‑2 infection and can lower quality of life.
author: Medical Xpress

title: NHS trials AI phone assistant Dora Care for osteoporosis patient monitoring
content:
An AI assistant that conducts telephone consultations is being trialed in the NHS to aid clinicians in monitoring patients with long‑term illness.  

The virtual assistant, named Dora Care, is designed to deliver safe and empathetic phone calls to people with osteoporosis. Osteoporosis is a bone‑weakening condition that affects 3.5 million people in the United Kingdom, especially women and those over 50. The trial will evaluate how Dora Care supports ongoing patient monitoring and clinician workload.
summary: An AI assistant called Dora Care is being trialed in the NHS to conduct telephone consultations with patients. The virtual assistant is designed to deliver safe, empathetic phone calls for people with osteoporosis, a bone‑weakening condition that affects 3.5 million people in the UK, particularly women and those over 50.
author: Medical Xpress

title: U. N. says global warming is going to exceed 1.5°C as scientists note rate doubled
content:
This year is being described as a potential turning point in the climate crisis. The United Nations has formally acknowledged that global warming is set to surpass the 1.5 °C threshold.  

Climate scientists report that the pace of warming has effectively doubled over the past decade.
summary: This year may be seen as a turning point in the climate crisis. The U.

title: Noise pollution alters biology or behavior in 80% of studied animal species
content: A study reports that noise pollution alters the biology or behavior of 80 % of the animal species examined. The article notes that sources such as traffic, ship rumble and heavy‑industry hum make escaping noise difficult, except for a hermit on a desert island.
summary: Noise pollution changes biology or behavior in 80% of animal species studied. The article notes that traffic, ships and heavy industry create pervasive noise, leaving few places without it.
author: Phys.org

title: Kyushu University develops smart film that glows under UV as meat spoils
content: Food spoilage produces chemical changes that are not always visible by appearance alone. Researchers at Kyushu University have created a smart packaging film that changes color and glows under ultraviolet (UV) light as meat loses freshness. When tested with refrigerated mutton, the film responds to compounds released during spoilage, providing two distinct ways to monitor changes in food quality. The study’s results were published in the Chemical Engineering Journal.
summary: Researchers at Kyushu University created a smart packaging film that changes color and glows under ultraviolet light as meat loses freshness. The film was tested with refrigerated mutton, responds to spoilage compounds, and the findings were published in the Chemical Engineering Journal.
author: Phys.org

title: AI framework seeks solid‑electrolyte discovery as lab results often fail in real batteries
content:
Researchers note that solid‑electrolyte materials can look perfect in the lab yet still fail in real batteries, presenting a key puzzle for those developing safer, longer‑lasting energy storage.  

A newly proposed AI‑driven framework seeks to move beyond trial‑and‑error approaches in solid‑electrolyte discovery, aiming to streamline the identification of viable battery materials.
summary: Researchers note that a battery material can appear perfect in the lab but still fail in a real battery. They propose a framework for AI‑driven solid‑electrolyte discovery to move beyond trial‑and‑error methods.
author: Phys.org

title: Francis Crick Institute finds lipid barrier helps fruit fly pupae resist dehydration
content: Researchers at the Francis Crick Institute have identified a specialized lipid barrier in fruit‑fly pupae that shields them from dehydration under dry, hot conditions. Their study also shows that this barrier has limits, implying that insects in certain regions could find it difficult to adapt as climate change intensifies.
summary: Researchers at the Francis Crick Institute identified a specialized lipid barrier in fruit fly pupae that protects against dehydration in dry and hot conditions. The study also indicates that the barrier’s limits could make insects in some regions struggle to adapt to climate change.
author: Phys.org

title: APOD November 7, 2026 Features De Gerlache‑Kocher Massif on Moon
content:
The Astronomy Picture of the Day for November 7, 2026 features a telescopic view of the De Gerla​che‑Kocher Massif on the Moon’s visible horizon. The close‑up image, captured on October 31, shows the mountainous formation rising roughly 4 kilometers above its surroundings near the lunar south pole. A favorable libration angle at the time of capture provided an oblique view across the pole.

The accompanying description notes that the massif’s permanently shadowed crater floors likely contain water‑ice deposits, while its peaks receive almost continuous sunlight, making the south‑polar region a prime candidate for the first human settlement on the Moon. The massif has also been mentioned as a potential landing site for future crewed Artemis missions.

The picture is credited to Alejandro Sanz, with the APOD entry authored and edited by Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, Robert Nemiroff and Keighley Rockcliffe. Tomorrow’s APOD image will focus on a meteoric subject.
summary: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 7 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.
author: NASA News

title: Midterm elections test Big Tech's shift from White House ties to courting Democrats
content: The piece notes that after two years of close ties with the White House, Big Tech is now seeking to build relationships with Democrats. It raises the question of whether this “image makeover” will survive the actions that states, local communities and the markets are poised to take, framing the issue in the context of the upcoming midterm elections.
summary: After two years of close ties with the White House, Big Tech is now seeking friendships with Democrats. The upcoming midterms raise questions about whether this image makeover can withstand actions by states, local communities and markets.

title: Sequoia shuts down its Scouts program, marking the model's decline
content: Sequoia is shutting down its Scouts program, an action described as marking the end of an era. The firm originally pioneered the scouts model, which was later adopted by many venture‑capital firms, and a consensus now appears that the model has reached limits in its current form.
summary: Sequoia is shutting down its Scouts program, a model it pioneered that many VC firms later followed. A consensus is forming that the scouts model has reached limits in its current form.
author: TechCrunch

title: Cyber‑attack heats European supermarket freezers, causing food loss worth millions
content: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up, many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers. Governments regularly warn retailers and other companies about cyber-attacks and even provide cyber-defence training to businesses. The lessons of costly ransomware and cyber-attacks also mean many big organisations and retailers have become much better at keeping their payments and logistics systems safe. Elisabeth Braw is a Swedish security expert and the author of The Undersea War : The International Battle for Supremacy at the Bottom of the World
summary: A cyber‑attack switched supermarket freezers from “freeze” to “defrost” across Europe, raising temperatures to about 50 °C and forcing the disposal of food worth millions of euros. Russian hacktivists claimed responsibility, though Iran, North Korea or unaffiliated hackers are also possible, and a similar hack previously hit Transport for London by two British teenagers.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Samuel Gibbs Tests AI Thermostats Over Two Years, Finds Unexpected Results
content:
Samuel Gibbs questioned whether technology could cut heating costs while keeping his home warm. He spent two years comparing his own manual heating schedule with an AI‑governed system. The results, he says, surprised him, suggesting that the AI approach may be more effective than he had expected.  

Manufacturers often claim average savings of around 25 % or £180 a year, but they also note heavy caveats. With energy prices fluctuating, it can be hard to determine what factors truly influence bill reductions. Gibbs’ experiment aimed to isolate the impact of smart thermostats and AI control on real‑world heating costs.
summary: Samuel Gibbs spent two years comparing a manual heating schedule to an AI‑governed system. The results surprised him, indicating that the AI approach may reduce heating costs.
author: Guardian Technology

title: UAE senior energy official says diversification ensures reliable supply to Europe
content: One of the UAE's most senior energy officials told Euronews diversification has carried the country's energy sector through months of regional crisis, as Europe looks to the Gulf for secure supply.
summary: A senior UAE energy official told Euronews that diversification has carried the country's energy sector through months of regional crisis. The official said the UAE will remain a reliable energy supplier as Europe looks to the Gulf for secure supply.

title: New Zealand counts votes in razor‑thin election after cost‑of‑living campaign
content:
New Zealand is currently counting ballots in a razor‑thin election that followed a campaign focused on the cost of living.  

In the country’s general election voters cast two separate votes: an electorate vote for a local candidate to represent their constituency in Parliament, and a party vote for the political party they wish to see in government.
summary: New Zealand is counting votes in a razor‑thin general election that followed a campaign centred on the cost of living. Voters cast a party vote for the government and an electorate vote for a local candidate.
author: Euronews

title: US Secret Service arrests man with multiple guns parked near White House
content: The US Secret Service arrested a man who was parked near the White House with “multiple guns” in his vehicle. According to the Department of Homeland Security, the suspect has been charged with several offenses, including possession of dangerous weapons and theft, and is now in the custody of the US Marshals Service.
summary: The US Secret Service arrested a man who was parked near the White House with multiple guns in his vehicle. He has been charged with possession of dangerous weapons and theft and is in the custody of the US Marshals Service.

title: Paraguay puts ousted President Santiago Peña under house arrest after banking crisis
content: Paraguayan authorities placed former president Santiago Peña under house arrest on Friday, days after the Senate voted unanimously to remove him from office because of a banking crisis that left nearly half of Paraguay’s population unable to access their savings. Peña had offered to resign over the scandal, but lawmakers proceeded with impeachment that removed his political immunity.
summary: Paraguayan authorities placed ousted president Santiago Peña under house arrest on Friday, shortly after the Senate unanimously removed him from office over a massive banking crisis that left nearly half of Paraguayans unable to access their savings. Peña had offered his resignation, but lawmakers continued impeachment proceedings that stripped him of political immunity.
author: France 24

title: Russia conducts missile and drone strike on Kyiv, kills one, injures eight
content: Moscow launched missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and its surrounding region overnight from Friday to Saturday, striking energy infrastructure. Authorities reported at least one death and eight injuries. The strikes come as Russia has recently intensified air attacks on Ukraine, further limiting residents’ access to power and water.
summary: Moscow carried out missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight Friday to Saturday, targeting energy infrastructure and killing at least one person while injuring eight, authorities said. Russia has recently stepped up air strikes on Ukraine, worsening living conditions for residents with limited access to power and water.

content: French unions and student groups are preparing to stage street protests on Saturday, while the Yellow Vests movement intends to hold a separate rally in central Paris despite a ban imposed by authorities. The actions come after weeks of youth‑led unrest and nationwide strikes that attracted hundreds of thousands of workers protesting the rising cost of living. The liveblog will provide ongoing updates on the demonstrations.
summary: French unions and student groups will protest on Saturday, and the Yellow Vests plan a separate rally in central Paris despite a ban by authorities. content: Democratic lawmakers have pledged to investigate former President Donald Trump, according to a report by Antonia Kerrigan. In the same statement, they said their agenda will focus on addressing the rising cost of living, probing alleged corruption and increasing oversight of ICE agents.

title: Yemen market attack in Taiz kills at least 30, blame disputed
content:
At least 30 people were killed in an attack on a market in Yemen’s Taiz province, according to reports. Houthi rebels attribute the strike to Saudi air operations, while government forces and local authorities reject that claim and say the Houthis fired indiscriminately.

The incident comes as the province endures intense clashes that have displaced more than 300,000 people, with roughly half of those displaced residing in Taiz. The report was filed by Caroline Baum.
summary: At least 30 people were killed in an attack on a market in Yemen’s Taiz province. Houthi rebels blamed Saudi airstrikes, while government forces and local authorities accused the Houthis of indiscriminate fire.

content: France intends to allocate an additional €4 billion to education while the country experiences nationwide protests. At the same time, public debt is rising and the cost of servicing that debt is increasing, prompting questions about the government’s remaining fiscal flexibility.

content: Russia carried out airstrikes on Kyiv, striking a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Moscow was attempting to push Ukraine into a blackout ahead of upcoming trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi.
