title: Probation warns early‑release prisoners may become homeless as temporary housing ends
content:
Charities say the case of a 37‑year‑old man named James highlights a “fatal flaw” in the plan announced by Andy Burnham to end rough sleeping in England by Christmas. James was released from prison in August and placed in temporary probation accommodation in Somerset, which is set to end in four days, leaving him with no housing options.

He told reporters that he has contacted MPs, solicitors, probation and the council but received no help, and he is considering asking to be recalled to prison as November’s cold weather approaches. Probation staff have warned that early‑release prisoners like James are at risk of street homelessness.
summary: Charities say the situation exposes a fatal flaw in Andy Burnham’s plan to end rough sleeping in England by Christmas. A 37‑year‑old man released in August faces street homelessness in four days after his temporary probation accommodation in Somerset expires, prompting him to consider returning to prison.
author: Guardian World

title: TikTok used by OnlyFans performers to covertly market sex industry to girls
content: Researchers say popular performers covertly market OnlyFans content and tell followers about wealthy lifestyle TikTok is helping to promote and normalise the sex industry, allowing “sexfluencers” to post videos aimed at marketing pornographic content they have uploaded elsewhere on sites such as OnlyFans, a report indicates. After studying non-explicit content posted on TikTok over the course of a year by some of OnlyFans’ most popular young female performers, researchers said the women buried coded references to pornography in “girly lifestyle content” that showed them shopping, playing with their pets, baking or offering skincare advice.
summary: TikTok used by OnlyFans performers to covertly market sex industry to girls.

title: US conducts another round of minor strikes on Iran, says Trump
content:
President Donald Trump announced that the U.S. military carried out a new round of limited strikes on Iran on Friday, targeting an air‑defence system and describing the action as “minor.” The statement followed an earlier attack on Iran that had been made public days earlier, as diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have accelerated.

Iranian state media reported hearing two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which lies in the Strait of Hormuz—a key oil‑shipping route that has been disrupted since the start of the U.S. war on Iran in February.
summary: President Donald Trump said the US military on Friday carried out a new round of limited strikes on Iran, targeting an air defence system and describing the action as minor. Iranian state media reported two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
author: Guardian World

title: Qatar plan may reopen Strait of Hormuz by urging Iran to permit UN nuclear inspections
content:
The headline indicates that the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened as part of a Qatari‑led plan to permit nuclear inspections in Iran.  

Qatar, identified as the lead mediator in the U.S.–Iran dispute, is working to persuade Tehran to allow United Nations nuclear‑weapons inspectors into Iran’s bombed nuclear facilities, including sites that house the country’s highly enriched uranium stockpile. The proposal does not require Iran to commit to removing the stockpile, and alternatives such as down‑blending the uranium to reduce its enrichment are being considered. Meanwhile, reports note that former President Trump is still weighing a new assault on Iran’s nuclear sites, though his threats are described as less credible after remarks by Vance.
summary: Qatar, the lead mediator in the US‑Iran conflict, is urging Tehran to allow UN nuclear weapons inspectors into Iran’s bombed nuclear sites that house its highly enriched uranium stockpile. The proposal, which does not require Iran to remove the stockpile and includes options such as down‑blending, could lead to the Strait of Hormuz reopening.
author: Guardian World

title: Home Office sued over loss of pre-settled status for nearly 1,500 EU citizens
content:
The Home Office is being sued for an alleged breach of the Brexit withdrawal agreement after it removed the full residency rights of nearly 1,500 EU citizens. The legal action follows reports that individuals who had been granted pre‑settled status to remain in the United Kingdom were later told the decisions were an “error”.

Campaign group the3million filed the court papers at the High Court on Friday, citing several cases in which the affected EU citizens had their pre‑settled status revoked. The group’s filing seeks to challenge the Home Office’s actions under the terms of the withdrawal agreement.
summary: Home Office sued over loss of pre-settled status for nearly 1,500 EU citizens.
author: Guardian World

title: Brazil removes emission‑cut plans from 2025 climate summit agenda as Paris goal missed
content: Its key temperature goal has been missed but experts say the agreement is still proving a vital moral compass for progress It was a curious way of conducting negotiations. Ahead of the 2025 climate summit, in the Amazonian port of Belém last year, the Brazilian hosts had taken off the table the issue that most had assumed would be at its heart: concrete plans from each country laying out exactly what they would be doing to cut their greenhouse gas emissions. Brazil was insisting, instead, that these plans – the bedrock of the Paris agreement – were the business of national governments and not up for negotiation. “In that case, it will be a very short Cop,” one seasoned global south negotiator told the Guardian shortly before, reflecting a widespread unease. “There is nothing to negotiate.”
summary: Experts say the Paris agreement’s key temperature goal has been missed but it remains a vital moral compass for progress. Ahead of the 2025 climate summit in Belém, Brazil said concrete emission‑reduction plans are a national issue and should not be negotiated.
author: Guardian World

title: New Zealand 2026 election live: National leads Labour, minor party poised as kingmaker
content:
Live results from New Zealand’s 2026 election show a remarkably close contest, with polls indicating that no coalition is likely to secure a majority of seats. The race has drawn attention to a minor party that could act as a kingmaker, turning the outcome into a potential cliffhanger.

At 8 % of the vote counted, the standings are: National 31.2 %, Labour 28.4 %, the Greens 12.9 %, Act 11.2 %, NZ First 9.6 %, Opportunity 5.7 % and Te Pāti Māori 0.4 %. According to these figures, a right‑bloc coalition would return to power, though a long way remains to reach a majority.
summary: New Zealand 2026 election live: National leads Labour, minor party poised as kingmaker.
author: Guardian World

title: SpaceX launches classified USSF-432 mission from Vandenberg
content:
SpaceX executed a classified launch for the U.S. Space Force on November 6, sending a Falcon 9 rocket into orbit from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. The liftoff occurred at 7:48 p.m. EST, coinciding with a sunset over the Pacific Ocean. Designated as the USSF-432 mission, the flight remained largely undisclosed by both SpaceX and the Space Force prior to launch. During the broadcast, SpaceX ended its webcast approximately ten minutes into the flight, shortly after the rocket’s first stage separated and began its return to Earth.

The Falcon 9’s first stage, booster 1095, successfully landed on the SpaceX droneship “Of Course I Still Love You,” which was positioned downrange in the Pacific Ocean. This event marked the eighth flight for this specific booster. Meanwhile, the rocket’s upper stage continued its ascent, carrying a mystery payload that observers speculate may be destined for low Earth orbit. External analysts suggest the payload could be a batch of classified satellites for the Space Force’s Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, potentially built on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite bus.

This launch represented the 119th Falcon 9 mission of 2026 and the 14th national-security flight for the rocket that year. In 2026, more than 70% of Falcon 9 missions have been dedicated to expanding the Starlink megaconstellation, which currently includes more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a related system designed to provide services to the U.S. Military and its allies, with satellites believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus.

Beyond the Falcon 9, SpaceX has conducted six other missions in 2026. These include three operational flights of the Falcon Heavy rocket and three test missions of the next-generation Starship vehicle. The company plans to retire both the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets once the fully reusable Starship, described as the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, is fully operational.
summary: SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U. S.
author: Space.com

title: Manchester United host Aston Villa in Premier League weekend action
content: Manchester United will host Aston Villa on Saturday at 12:30pm, with the match set to air on TNT Sports 1. The Red Devils are aiming for their first league victory in eight games to ease pressure on manager Michael Carrick. The fixture is scheduled to take place at Elland Road.
summary: Manchester United will host Aston Villa on Saturday at 12.30pm on TNT Sports 1. The match is scheduled to take place at Elland Road as United seeks a first league win in eight games.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Matthias Jaissle faces criticism as Newcastle struggle without European football
content:
Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle faces growing criticism from fans as the club struggles to adapt to life without Champions League participation. Speaking on Thursday, Jaissle acknowledged the current turmoil, stating, “There’s a lot of storm at the moment,” while reportedly maintaining the support of the club’s hierarchy. The article notes that Jaissle’s tactics, team selection, and management philosophy have been heavily criticized in recent days, yet he appears to be holding his nerve.

The piece attributes the heightened pressure to the club’s 12th-place finish under Eddie Howe last season, which resulted in the loss of European competition and the associated financial benefits. Without the “continental fix” of trips to cities like Barcelona, Paris, and Marseille, Newcastle is finding the transition difficult. The article uses an analogy to describe the current mindset, comparing the situation to a passenger accustomed to business class who is suddenly stuck in a cramped economy seat as they prepare to travel to Fulham on Saturday.
summary: Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle is facing intense scrutiny over his tactics and team selection as the club adjusts to life without Champions League involvement. The team travels to Fulham on Saturday amid fan discontent stemming from the loss of European fixtures and associated financial benefits.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Charlton’s eight-game losing streak highlights gap between WSL and second tier
content: Pointless after eight games, Karen Hills’ team are struggling to compete against clubs with chunkier wallets Played eight, lost eight. Welcome to the Women’s Super League, Charlton Athletic, a club in danger of being chewed up, toyed with and spat straight back out by the top tier. Bruised by their 6-0 defeat against Chelsea on Sunday, last season’s playoff winners are finding WSL life tough, conceding more than three goals per game on average and struggling to compete against clubs with chunkier wallets. But are they underperforming or are they merely the victims of their own success?
summary: Charlton Athletic have lost all eight of their Women’s Super League games, including a 6-0 defeat against Chelsea. The article suggests the team is struggling to compete against clubs with larger budgets despite winning the previous season's playoffs.
author: Guardian Sport

title: USA women beat Switzerland 7-0 to open hockey worlds in Denmark
content:
The United States women’s ice hockey team opened their defense of the world championship with a 7-0 victory over Switzerland on Friday in Esbjerg, Denmark. Hannah Bilka and Laila Edwards each scored twice, while Kirsten Simms, Hilary Knight, and Casey O’Brien also found the net. The Americans pulled away from a competitive opening period, with Caroline Harvey contributing three assists to the rout.

The tournament’s Danish debut was overshadowed by a jersey dispute. Meanwhile, Canada opened its campaign with a 5-1 win over Sweden, during which Eldridge shined.
summary: The United States defeated Switzerland 7-0 on Friday in Esbjerg, Denmark, to open their defense of the women's ice hockey world championship. Hannah Bilka and Laila Edwards scored twice each, while Kirsten Simms, Hilary Knight, and Casey O'Brien also found the net.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Knicks defend Taylor Swift after players label her a “fake fan”
content: Kolek calls singer’s courtside appearances ‘performative’ McBride agrees as teammates question celebrity fandom Knicks give statement saying Swift is longtime supporter Taylor Swift’s love story with the New York Knicks caught an unexpected stray after two players from last season’s NBA champions accused the singer of being a fair-weather fan. The Knicks released a statement on Friday defending Swift after Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride questioned whether the pop superstar was a genuine supporter of the team.
summary: The New York Knicks released a statement on Friday defending Taylor Swift and calling her a longtime supporter of the team. Players Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride said her courtside appearances are “performative” and questioned whether she is a genuine fan.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Khawaja: Entire Australia team knew about 2018 sandpaper plot
content:
Usman Khawaja has claimed that the entire Australia touring party was aware of the 2018 ball-tampering plot against South Africa in Cape Town. The former Test opener stated that the team also used sandpaper on the cricket ball during the second Test in Port Elizabeth. According to Khawaja, this practice occurred before Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera handling the object during the third Test.

These remarks were made ahead of the release of Khawaja’s autobiography, Sabr, on Tuesday. Despite these allegations, Khawaja remains comfortable with the decision to issue bans only to David Warner, Steve Smith, and Cameron Bancroft.
summary: Former Test opener Usman Khawaja claims the entire Australia touring party knew about the ball tampering plot in Cape Town and also used sandpaper in Port Elizabeth. Khawaja states he remains comfortable with bans only for Bancroft, Warner, and Smith ahead of his autobiography release.
author: Guardian Sport

title: DOJ seeks to dismiss California lawsuit over 20,000 disputed ballots
content: The Justice Department requested Friday to dismiss its lawsuit against California, which sought to compel state election officials to set aside approximately 20,000 ballots cast by individuals the federal government alleged were not U.S. citizens. The Supreme Court had previously ruled against the Trump administration in an emergency order issued ahead of Election Day.
summary: The Justice Department requested to dismiss its lawsuit against California, which sought to invalidate approximately 20,000 ballots cast by voters alleged to be non-citizens. The Supreme Court had previously ruled against the administration in an emergency order before Election Day.
author: The Hill

title: Genetic variant may increase pneumonia risk, study finds
content:
A new study published in eBioMedicine indicates that genetic differences within the innate immune system can influence the risk of developing pneumonia. Researchers from Lund University and Skåne University Hospital conducted this investigation, adding a genetic dimension to the understanding of the disease.

Pneumonia is a common and sometimes serious infection that affects 20,000–30,000 people annually in Sweden. While advanced age, smoking, and underlying medical conditions are well-known risk factors, the study highlights that genetic variants may also play a significant role in susceptibility to the infection.
summary: Researchers at Lund University and Skåne University Hospital found that genetic differences in the innate immune system can influence the risk of developing pneumonia. The study, published in eBioMedicine, adds to known risk factors such as advanced age, smoking, and underlying medical conditions.
author: Medical Xpress

title: AI smartwatch detects high blood pressure with sensitivity similar to office screening
content: A paper in Nature reports that an AI system can detect hypertension by interpreting sensor readings from a consumer smartwatch. Tests of the system show it achieves sensitivities similar to traditional office-based blood pressure screening methods.
summary: A paper in Nature reports that an AI system can interpret smartwatch sensor readings to detect hypertension. Tests using a consumer smartwatch show the system detects high blood pressure with sensitivity similar to traditional office-based screening methods.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Liver Drug Added to World's Largest Parkinson's Trial to Slow Disease Progression
content: A liver drug is set to join the world's largest clinical trial for Parkinson's disease treatments. The medication is being considered for its potential to slow the progression of the condition.
summary: A liver drug could be used to slow down the progression of Parkinson's disease. It has joined the world's largest trial of Parkinson's treatments.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Gene therapy shows sustained efficacy four years after treatment for Crigler-Najjar syndrome
content:
The New England Journal of Medicine has published a study evaluating the long‑term efficacy of AAV8‑mediated gene therapy (GNT0003) in patients with Crigler‑Najjar syndrome. The report shows that the therapy’s benefits are maintained four years after treatment.  

Crigler‑Najjar syndrome is an extremely rare congenital liver disorder that affects roughly 500 people in Europe. It results from a deficiency of the enzyme UGT1A1, which is required for bilirubin metabolism. When bilirubin accumulates, it can cause irreversible neurological damage and, in the most severe cases, death.
summary: The New England Journal of Medicine has published a study on the long-term efficacy of AAV8-mediated gene therapy (GNT0003) in patients with Crigler-Najjar syndrome, an extremely rare congenital liver disorder affecting approximately 500 people in Europe. It is caused by a deficiency of UGT1A1, an enzyme required for bilirubin metabolism.
author: Medical Xpress

title: South African trial tests off-the-shelf killer cells against lymphoma
content: South African researchers are testing "off-the-shelf" immune cells against lymphoma that has relapsed or resisted prior treatment. This approach investigates a method that avoids manufacturing individualized therapies from each patient’s own cells.
summary: South African researchers are testing "off-the-shelf" immune cells against lymphoma that has returned or resisted treatment, investigating an approach that avoids having to manufacture a separate treatment from each patient's own cells.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Bariatric surgery effective after GLP-1 failure, study finds
content: A study published in the Annals of Surgery on November 3 reports that bariatric surgery is an effective rescue strategy following the failure of GLP-1 receptor agonists. The research indicates that patients who underwent surgery after experiencing intolerance or an inadequate response to semaglutide or tirzepatide achieved clinically meaningful weight loss over a two-year period.
summary: A study published in the Annals of Surgery found that bariatric surgery is associated with clinically meaningful two-year weight loss. This outcome occurs after patients experience intolerance or an inadequate response to semaglutide or tirzepatide.
author: Medical Xpress

title: AI helps Texas A&M AgriLife Research scientists identify new disease targets in mitochondria
content: Artificial intelligence is assisting Texas A&M AgriLife Research scientists in rapidly addressing a long‑standing question in human biology: determining the functions of hundreds of mystery proteins located in the mitochondria. The AI tool helps accelerate the identification of these proteins’ roles.
summary: Artificial intelligence is assisting Texas A&M AgriLife Research scientists in answering a long-standing question about the function of hundreds of mystery proteins in mitochondria. This work is helping researchers fast-track the discovery of new disease targets hidden within these cellular structures.
author: Phys.org

title: Elon Musk Criticizes Nolan's Odyssey Adaptation, Launches AI to Produce Accurate Film
content: Tech billionaire Elon Musk was up in arms about the recent adaptation of Homer's "Odyssey" by director Christopher Nolan, which he heavily criticized for its diverse casting and accused of lacking historical accuracy. Claiming he wanted to show that artificial intelligence could bypass traditional Hollywood studios and deliver a story "historically accurate and true to the art of Homer" at a fraction of the cost, he set his AI Grok Imagine to the task.
summary: Elon Musk criticized Christopher Nolan's recent adaptation of Homer's Odyssey for its diverse casting and lack of historical accuracy. Musk announced he would use his AI Grok Imagine to create a historically accurate film at a lower cost.
author: Phys.org

title: High-precision timeline helps clarify an ancient magma surge in the North Cascades
content: A new high‑precision timeline has shed light on an ancient magma surge that occurred in the North Cascades. The study focuses on continental arcs, which form where oceanic crust subducts beneath continental crust. These arcs can experience episodic magma flare‑ups, with magma flow into the continental crust increasing up to 20 times the normal rate. The surges can last tens of millions of years, but the exact triggers for these extreme events remain unclear.
summary: Where oceanic crust subducts beneath continental crust, belts of volcanoes known as continental arcs can form. Located around the world, these arcs may undergo episodic magma flare-ups—dramatic surges in the flow of magma into the continental crust at rates up to 20 times higher than normal.
author: Phys.org

title: European forests must tackle two crises, not necessarily together
content: Forest areas can serve as both carbon sinks and vital habitats for thousands of species, but not always simultaneously. A University of Copenhagen researcher notes that this dual role creates important implications for how Europe should manage its forests.
summary: Forest areas can serve as both carbon sinks and habitats for thousands of species, but not simultaneously. A University of Copenhagen researcher says this has important implications for how Europe should manage its forests.
author: Phys.org

title: Untangling Cosmic Microwave Background Patterns to Understand Early Universe
content: Scientists are working to untangle patterns in the cosmic microwave background to better understand the early universe. In a recent illustration, a figure in red trudges across a white blanket of snow, with flags and large buildings marking the destination. The sun hovers on a cloudless blue horizon as the snow squeaks underfoot.
summary: A scientist in red trudges across a snowy landscape toward a line of flags and large buildings. The snow squeaks under their feet while the sun hovers on a cloudless blue horizon.
author: Phys.org

title: 480,000 Trucks Haul 4.8 Million Tons of Rubble in Jamaica After Hurricane Melissa
content:
Hurricane Melissa tore through western Jamaica in 2025, leaving extensive rubble.  
United Nations satellites showed that about 480,000 trucks hauled 4.8 million metric tons (5.3 million tons) of debris across the area.
summary: United Nations satellites showed that it took around 480,000 trucks to haul away 4.8 million metric tons of rubble across western Jamaica after Hurricane Melissa. Hurricane Melissa tore through the Caribbean in 2025.
author: Phys.org

title: OpenAI Valued at $1.25 Trillion After New $11B Funding Round
content:
OpenAI has been valued at $1.25 trillion after a new funding round that raised $11 billion, Bloomberg reports. The valuation places the company among the world’s most valuable firms.

Bloomberg echoes reports from the Financial Times and the Wall Street Journal that OpenAI is still pursuing additional investments that could raise the total to $20 billion. The company had originally aimed to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation before tech stocks fell and midterm election results influenced market sentiment.
summary: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round of funding that has raised another $11 billion, according to Bloomberg. That would make it one of the world's most valuable companies, not long after raising $122 billion from investors in March at a valuation of $852 billion.
author: The Verge

title: EA re-releases 25 classic games including Wing Commander and Ultima on Steam and GOG
content:
Many gamers are currently critical of game publisher EA, a sentiment that has grown in recent years. For those who recall the company’s more celebrated 1990s releases, there is a modest point of optimism.  

Twenty‑five classic titles from EA’s earlier catalog have been lightly remastered and updated. These games are now available for purchase on Steam and GOG, with the collection featuring several Wing Commander titles and nearly the entire Ultima series.  

A complete list of the remastered or re‑released games is provided in the full article, with comments available for readers.
summary: EA has placed 25 lightly remastered classic games from its 1990s catalog on Steam and GOG. The releases include several Wing Commander titles and nearly the entire Ultima series.
author: Ars Technica

title: Iran-linked tankers loiter near Gulf of Oman undersea cables amid warnings to Trump
content:
Several tanker ships linked to Iran have been observed loitering over subsea Internet cables in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz. Maritime intelligence firm Windward tracked the movements of three sanctioned tankers and an Iranian fishing boat in October, according to the Financial Times. The activity has been described as a possible indication that the Iranian government is preparing to attack undersea infrastructure in response to any renewed U.S. and Israeli strikes.

Six active cables currently cross the contested Strait of Hormuz, connecting the Middle East with Europe, Africa and Asia. Two additional cables have segments under construction in the region. Four countries—Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar—depend entirely on subsea telecommunications links that run through the Strait to reach the outside world. Other nations also rely heavily on the region’s cable network; for example, one‑third of India’s westbound Internet traffic passes through the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.
summary: Three sanctioned tankers and an Iranian fishing boat were tracked by Windward near major undersea cables in the Gulf of Oman in October. The movements suggest Iran may be preparing to attack subsea infrastructure in response to potential US and Israeli strikes.
author: Ars Technica

title: UK man in his 20s survives knife through eye and brain, remains conscious
content:
A man in his 20s arrived at a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife protruding from his face. The 15 mm‑wide blade had passed completely through his right eye and brain, with the tip reaching the top of his skull. Despite the injury, he was alive, conscious, able to speak and move all four limbs, though he was described as agitated.

Medical staff assessed his neurological status with the Glasgow Coma Scale, recording a score of 12 (E3 V4 M5), indicating a moderate brain injury. Because his confused and agitated condition raised the risk that he might attempt to remove the knife himself, doctors promptly sedated and intubated him, administered prophylactic treatments for bacterial infection including tetanus, and obtained imaging to evaluate the damage.

The case was detailed in a report published on Friday in BMJ Case Report. The report outlines the immediate clinical decisions made to stabilize the patient and prevent further harm while assessing the extent of his injuries.
summary: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm-wide blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull.
author: Ars Technica

title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future uncertain after midterms setback
content: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future is in question after Tuesday's, November 3, midterms setback. On Thursday, November 5, he issued a video message vowing to fight efforts in Congress to impeach him and defending the ‌Iran war as “courageous and historic”. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.
summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future uncertain after midterms setback.
author: France 24

title: Gadi Eisenkot emerges as frontrunner to form Israeli government on Nov 5
content: Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday, November 5, as the leading candidate to be tasked with forming Israel’s next government, according to France 24’s Jerusalem correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky. His rise follows the refusal of one of the two main ultra‑Orthodox parties—an ally of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition—to recommend a candidate for the role.
summary: Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday, November 5 as the frontrunner to be tasked with forming a government in Israel. One of the two main parties representing ultra‑Orthodox Jewish voters, a longtime ally of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, declined to recommend any candidate for the task.
author: France 24

title: Russian diesel tankers abandon US delivery under Trump‑Putin deal
content: The first oil tankers that had been slated to bring Russian diesel to the United States under a deal announced by President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin have altered their routes and are no longer heading toward the U.S. coast, effectively ending the agreement that was publicized with great fanfare before the midterm elections.
summary: The first oil tankers scheduled to deliver Russian diesel to the United States under a deal between President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin have changed course and are no longer heading toward the US coast. The shift spells the end of the agreement that was announced with great fanfare before the midterms.
author: France 24

title: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña submits resignation amid banking scandal and protests
content: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña submitted his resignation on Thursday, but Congress delayed its acceptance as impeachment proceedings continue. Peña faces impeachment tied to a banking scandal that has impacted millions and triggered recent protests, with thousands gathering in the streets.
summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña submitted his resignation on Thursday. Congress has put the resignation on hold while impeachment proceedings continue over a banking scandal that has affected millions and sparked protests.
author: France 24

title: Bomb threat hoaxes hit European airlines, no explosives found
content:
Irish media outlets reported receiving bomb threats on Friday, part of a broader wave of hoax alerts that have primarily targeted airlines across Europe. The latest incidents have affected more than a dozen flights, though no explosives have been discovered in any of the cases.

European authorities are working to identify the sources of the threats, according to FRANCE 24’s Brussels correspondent Dave Keating. The situation remains under investigation, and officials caution that it is too early to draw conclusions.
summary: Several Irish media outlets received bomb threats on Friday as a wave of hoax alerts targeting airlines across Europe affected more than a dozen flights. No explosives have been found and European authorities are scrambling to identify the sources of the threats, according to FRANCE 24's Brussels correspondent Dave Keating.
author: France 24

title: The women who rode the blue wave
content:
The latest edition notes that the recent U.S. midterm elections, in which Democrats achieved massive gains, also produced a series of historic firsts for women, highlighting their expanding role in the political landscape.

It also examines the darker aspects of Bangkok’s booming fertility industry, which draws thousands of foreign patients to the city’s state‑of‑the‑art private clinics.

Finally, the issue reports on an impoverished neighbourhood in El Salvador that was once a no‑go zone plagued by gang violence; women are now reshaping the area into a vibrant canvas for street art.
summary: In this edition, we report on how the US midterms, which saw the Democrats make massive gains, also marked a series of historic firsts for women. Also the dark side to Bangkok's booming fertility industry, which attracts thousands of foreign patients seeking assistance from the Thai capital's state-of-the-art private clinics.
author: France 24

title: California Governor Gavy Newsom to commute sentences of all 548 death row inmates
content: California Governor Gavy Newsom announced Thursday that he will grant clemency to all 548 death‑row inmates, commuting every death sentence in the state to life without the possibility of parole. He said “capital punishment is morally wrong.” The state Supreme Court will retain final authority over hundreds of the resulting cases.
summary: California Governor Gavy Newsom announced Thursday that he will commute the sentences of all 548 death row inmates to life without the possibility of parole. He said capital punishment is morally wrong, and the state Supreme Court will have the final say in hundreds of the cases.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV begins Latin America tour with stop in Uruguay
content:
Pope Leo XIV begins a three‑nation Latin America tour on Friday, November 6, starting in Uruguay. Uruguay is described as the region’s least Catholic and most secular country.  

The trip follows Pope Leo XIV’s lung cancer surgery three weeks earlier, which had raised doubts about the itinerary. After Uruguay, the Pope will visit Argentina and Peru. Source: FRANCE 24’s Hanna Roberts.
summary: Pope Leo XIV is beginning a three‑nation Latin American tour on Friday, November 6, with a visit to Uruguay, the region’s least Catholic and most secular country. The trip follows his lung cancer surgery three weeks earlier and will continue to Argentina and Peru.
author: France 24

title: Susie Wiles exits White House as Trump ousts another woman from key role
content: Wiles thanks president for ‘honor of a lifetime’ as departure leaves behind overwhelmingly male leadership team US politics live – latest updates Donald Trump on Friday said Susie Wiles, the first woman to serve as White House chief of staff, will leave her post, a major shake-up of his inner circle that comes amid a steady exodus of senior female officials from his administration. The president announced her ouster – and her replacement, by the immigration hardliner Stephen Miller – in a post on Truth Social, days after a sweeping blue wave gave Democrats control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections. Wiles’s departure leaves behind an overwhelmingly male leadership team.
summary: Susie Wiles exits White House as Trump ousts another woman from key role.
author: Guardian World

title: Man in custody after being found in vehicle near White House with guns
content:
A man was taken into custody and charged after U.S. Secret Service officers discovered him in a vehicle parked near the White House with multiple firearms. The suspect, Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, was described as “acting suspicious” and was approached by officers on Thursday night.  

According to a Homeland Security statement, Guanipa Chrinos told officers that voices in his head were instructing him to come to the nation's capital and kill the Republican president. The Secret Service confirmed the arrest and the charges following the discovery of the armed vehicle.
summary: Man in custody after being found in vehicle near White House with guns.
author: Guardian World

title: Trump names Stephen Miller chief of staff after voters reject deportation push
content:
U.S. voters on Tuesday rebuked Donald Trump’s mass‑deportation campaign, describing it as “brutal” and noting that it deployed military tanks and masked agents through residential streets.  

Four days later, on Friday, President Trump announced the appointment of Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff. Miller is identified in the announcement as the architect of the administration’s most aggressive immigration policies.
summary: On Tuesday, US voters resoundingly rebuked Donald Trump and his mass deportation campaign that sent military tanks and masked agents through residential streets. On Friday, Trump named Stephen Miller, the architect of the administration’s most aggressive immigration policies, as his new chief of staff.
author: Guardian World

title: Stephen Miller, architect of Trump immigration crackdown, named White House chief of staff
content:
The president announced that Stephen Miller will become White House chief of staff. Miller, described as Donald Trump’s most controversial aide and the architect of the former president’s sweeping immigration crackdown, will replace Susie Wiles.

Wiles, the current chief of staff and the first woman to hold the post, will step down. The appointment was confirmed on Friday, coming days after Republicans lost control of the U.S. Congress in the midterm elections.
summary: President announced on Friday that Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Miller, the architect of Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, assumes the role days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections.
author: Guardian World

title: Democrats condemn Trump’s appointment of Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff
content: Chuck Schumer says the move to promote the controversial immigration hardliner shows that Donald Trump ‘learned nothing from his historic defeat’ in the midterms Stephen Miller, architect of Trump’s immigration crackdown, to become White House chief of staff Sign up for Breaking News US email Donald Trump will begin the day in Washington today. title: Ben Roberts-Smith collaborates with gym business run by influencer that sold ‘war crimes’ pre-workout supplement
content:
Ben Roberts‑Smith has entered a collaboration with Zero Limits supplements, a gym‑supplements business co‑owned by right‑wing podcaster and fitness coach Chris Katelaris, who is also known as “Big Chocky”. The company recently marketed a pre‑workout product titled “war crimes”.

Roberts‑Smith, described as one of Australia’s most decorated living soldiers and currently awaiting trial on war‑crimes charges, has also launched an apparel brand called Epic 1 Two that produces T‑shirts and gym wear.
summary: Ben Roberts-Smith has collaborated with Zero Limits supplements, a gym supplement company co‑owned by right‑wing podcaster and fitness coach Chris Katelaris (“Big Chocky”). Roberts‑Smith, a highly decorated Australian soldier awaiting trial on war‑crimes charges, recently launched the apparel brand Epic 1 Two.
author: Guardian World

title: I finally got my hands on the Unistellar Envision smart binoculars with augmented reality and I can’t wait to stargaze with them
content:
The Unistellar Envision smart binoculars, announced in 2024, are the first pair of smart binoculars designed specifically for night sky observation. They feature an augmented reality (AR) overlay in the right-hand lens that identifies night sky targets, including planets, stars, and deep space objects, as well as landmarks and navigational tools. The device is pre-ordered for $1,499 or £1,299 and ships with a soft carry case, padded neck strap, USB-C cable, and rubber caps for the eyepieces and lenses.

The binoculars have a solid build, though they are not the most lightweight option due to the embedded technology. They feature 10x magnification and 50mm objective lenses, which provide strong light-gathering power essential for stargazing. The control panel includes five buttons on the top: the left side controls guided tour advancement, target lock selection, and display mode, while the right side houses the calibration and power buttons, with the power button also serving as a switch for the AR display. A central focus wheel allows for manual adjustments, though it requires two hands to operate.

Setting up the device is recommended during the daytime to allow time for familiarization with the controls and diopter adjustment. After powering on, the binoculars connect to the Unistellar app, which recognizes the device and provides onboarding videos. Users are advised to perform a 360-degree calibration before first use and to set location services to "always" to ensure accurate AR readings for target locations.

In daytime testing, the topographical identification feature successfully identified local landmarks, and the target lock feature allowed a friend to easily locate a geographical landmark via the AR indicator. However, the diopter adjustment is only accurate for one person at a time, making it inconvenient to swap users during field observation. Additionally, a friend had to adjust the focus wheel to make the AR overlay sharp enough to read, a minor inconvenience noted during testing.

The reviewer has not yet tested the night mode due to cloudy skies but anticipates using the device for stargazing and teaching others about constellations. The Unistellar Envision is expected to receive additional functionality through future software updates, with a plan to allow third-party app development in 2027. The device offers distinct modes for night observation, daytime use, and navigation, the latter displaying cardinal direction alongside azimuth and elevation angles.
summary: I have been waiting to get my hands on a pair of Unistellar Envision smart binoculars since they were announced in 2024. Our editor-in-chief tried an early demo of them last year and said that they felt like something out of Star Trek.
author: Space.com

title: German astronomer discovers Tycho supernova in 1572, initially mistaken for a new star
content: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572, is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia, was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004. "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time. Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis, or the Blaze Star, the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). Is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
summary: German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova in the constellation Cassiopeia with the naked eye on Nov. 6, 1572, though Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. The event, known as Tycho's Star, was visible to the naked eye for 16 months and was not classified as a supernova until the 1940s.
author: Space.com

title: Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook review – the heir to a legendary eatery … who sets soup on fire
content:
In the cooking series Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook, actor, rapper, and comedian Awkwafina navigates the kitchen with genuine bewilderment. Known by her real name, Nora Lum, within the series, she is portrayed as having no prior experience with culinary tools or techniques. The show documents her chaotic and humorous journey as she attempts to resurrect her family’s famous restaurant.

The review highlights the authenticity of Awkwafina’s lack of culinary knowledge, noting that her ignorance of how food, pans, knives, and plates work feels refreshing compared to other celebrity cooking shows where inexperience is often performed. Specific scenes illustrate her discomfort, including her crouched stance near the oven, her tentative handling of spatulas and ladles, and her visible aversion to raw ingredients.

The narrative describes her progression as chaotic, hilarious, and deeply moving. Despite her initial bafflement and fear of the kitchen environment, she valiantly works to restore the legacy of the eatery. The review concludes that her genuine inability to cook, rather than a staged act, provides a truthful and engaging foundation for the series.
summary: She is completely baffled in the kitchen, but the star valiantly resurrects her family’s famous restaurant. Her journey is chaotic, hilarious – and deeply moving It starts both very well and very badly does Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook.
author: Guardian Culture

title: U2 discuss new album Carnaval de Luz and Bono’s refusal to work with Trump
content: After some so-so albums, can U2’s new one, Carnaval de Luz, restore them to glory? They discuss male egos, working with Dolly Parton, and explain why, despite Trump, they still believe in democracy – at least in their band La Petite Maison, in Nice, has a certain reputation as a five-star celebrity haunt. Beyoncé eats here. So do Elton John, Tom Cruise, Harry Styles and Leonardo DiCaprio, their meals presided over by the restaurant’s founder, Nicole, variously described in print as “eccentric”, “unique” and “truculent” (she’s standing by the entrance when I arrive, and suffice to say, doesn’t look like someone you’d much enjoy being on the wrong side of). It’s enough of a celebrity haunt that the arrival of U2 – still incontrovertibly one of the biggest bands in the world 40 years after they could first reasonably have called themselves such – causes barely a murmur of interest among their fellow lunchtime diners. Then again, Bono is a regular. He was eating on the outdoor terrace the night of Nice’s terrorist attack, on Bastille Day in 2016, in which 86 people were killed. “I climbed through that window and hid under there,” he nods, pointing to a table at the rear of the restaurant. “Nicole,” he adds, “didn’t hide.”
summary: U2 discusses their new album, Carnaval de Luz, and explains why Bono cannot work with Donald Trump. The band also reflects on 50 years together and their continued belief in democracy within their group.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Macklemore says nine US arenas refused his Free Palestine tour
content:
Macklemore has claimed that nine major US arenas refused to host his Free Palestine fundraising tour, citing “intimidation, manipulation and suppression” in a social media post. The rapper stated that he intended to bring the tour to the United States but faced rejection from several prominent venues.

Among the locations named in his Instagram post are New York City’s Madison Square Garden, Los Angeles’s Crypto.com arena, and Brooklyn’s Barclays Center. Macklemore linked these refusals to the recent Ed Sheeran controversy, asserting that the venues declined to host his event.
summary: Macklemore said nine major US arenas refused to host his Free Palestine fundraising tour. He listed Madison Square Garden, Crypto. Com arena and Barclays Center as venues that turned him down.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Chilean director Sebastián Lelio, known for A Fantastic Woman, dies aged 52
content:
Sebastián Lelio, the Chilean director known for films such as Gloria and A Fantastic Woman, has died at the age of 52. The article describes him as a filmmaker of great passion and poetry who expertly captured both personal and political themes. Lelio is identified as one of the standard bearers of the Novisimo Cine Chileno, or New Chilean Cinema, a movement that includes directors Pablo Larraín, Patricio Guzmán, and Sebastián Silva.

The text notes that the last two decades have seen a significant rise in creativity from Chilean filmmakers. These directors brought global attention to the nation’s history, including the period of Augusto Pinochet’s rule, which the article characterizes as a tyranny enabled by the United States as an alternative to communism. The filmmakers also depicted the transition to a prosperous democratic normality where collective trauma and guilt persisted.

Lelio’s work is characterized as fierce, passionate, and sensual, with some films being explicitly political while others were not. The article argues that his films served as an expression of defiance against a system that deprived ordinary people of pleasure, effectively dramatizing the complex and conflicted zeitgeist of 21st-century Chile.
summary: Sebastián Lelio, the Chilean director of films including Gloria and A Fantastic Woman, has died at the age of 52. He was recognized for his passionate and sensual works that dramatized Chile's complex 21st-century zeitgeist.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd confirm split, reject WNBA draft influence claims
content:
Dallas Wings teammates Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd confirmed on Friday that they ended their romantic relationship more than a year ago. The former University of Connecticut teammates made the announcement during an episode of Fudd’s podcast, where they also addressed recent speculation. They specifically rejected claims that their personal relationship influenced the team’s decision to select Fudd with the No. 1 pick in this year’s WNBA draft.

In addition to clarifying the timeline of their split, the pair asked fans to stop sending hostile messages to them and their friends and family.
summary: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd confirmed on a podcast that they ended their romantic relationship more than a year ago. They rejected speculation that their relationship influenced the Dallas Wings' decision to select Fudd with the No. 1 pick in the WNBA draft.

title: Wallabies struggle to turn moments into momentum despite talented squad
content:
The Wallabies possess a squad with the potential for exceptional performances, yet questions persist regarding their ability to consistently translate individual talent into sustained team success. The team frequently demonstrates moments of brilliance, such as Len Ikitau’s underhand pass to Max Jorgensen for a late try at Twickenham and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii’s run past multiple British and Irish Lions defenders. Additionally, Australia has shown resilience in high-pressure situations, including securing a victory against the Springboks while down to 11 men and defending a four-point lead with five minutes remaining.

Despite these flashes of ability, the Wallabies have struggled to maintain this level of performance over extended periods. Historical context suggests that while previous Australian teams have exhibited similar sparks, few have managed to convert them into consistent wins across consecutive matches. Recent results reflect this inconsistency, as the team lost all four Tests on their European tour last autumn and suffered two additional defeats in the summer.

Following a successful unbeaten run of six matches against Italy, Japan, Argentina, and South Africa, the Wallabies faced significant setbacks in the Bledisloe Cup. They were defeated by the All Blacks in consecutive matches, losing by 31 points in one week and 22 points the following week. These results highlight the ongoing challenge for the team to turn isolated moments of excellence into lasting momentum and revive the spirits of the squad.
summary: The Wallabies possess individual talents capable of magic, but doubts remain about their ability to form a consistently winning team. Australia’s recent form includes losing all four European Tests and two consecutive Bledisloe Cup matches to the All Blacks.

title: Tuchel calls Jobe Bellingham to England squad after Jude's request
content: Jude had asked head coach to scout Dortmund midfielder ‘It will be beautiful for Jude to have his brother close’ Thomas Tuchel has given a first England call-up to Jobe Bellingham, admitting the midfielder’s older brother, Jude, had nagged him to do so, as he set up the prospect of their family dream being realised. Tuchel’s inclusion of the younger Bellingham for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain was further evidence of his shift away from the squad that served him well at the World Cup last summer and towards a fresh dynamic for the mission to win Euro 2028. The manager has named a 25-man group for the game against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday and the one against Spain in Madrid three days after; of the 22 outfield players, only 11 were at the World Cup.
summary: Thomas Tuchel has selected Jobe Bellingham for England's upcoming Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain. The manager admitted that Jude Bellingham had asked him to scout his younger brother, describing their potential reunion as a beautiful story.

title: Keenan hat-trick leads Ireland to 42-12 win over Argentina
content:
Ireland secured an emphatic 42-12 victory over Argentina in the Nations Championship, with Keenan scoring a hat-trick in a match that featured six tries for the Irish side. The result marked a significant win for Ireland as they opened November’s international window. In contrast, Argentina’s defeat was highlighted by Carreras, who scored twice for his team during the encounter.

The match was described as almost tame, a notable shift from the historically mean and nasty World Cup meetings between the two nations. Although the rivalry has never been friendly, ranging from uncapped affairs to full Test status, this particular contest lacked the previous intensity. The backdrop for the game included next year’s World Cup in Australia, where there is a decent chance of the two teams meeting again in the knockout stages. Should that scenario occur, Ireland will view complacency as their biggest enemy.
summary: Ireland defeated Argentina 42-12 in a Nations Championship match where Keenan scored a hat-trick. Argentina's Carreras scored twice during the defeat.

title: Thierno Barry scores twice as Everton beat Coventry
content:
Thierno Barry scored twice to lead Everton to a comeback victory over Coventry, securing the club’s third consecutive win. The striker’s second goal, which appeared to come off his arm, took his season total to 10 goals in all competitions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added a late goal to seal the result in convincing style.

The match featured two strong penalty shouts for Coventry that were dismissed, resulting in a torturous night for manager Frank Lampard against his old club. Despite a calamitous transfer window, Everton currently sits fifth in the Premier League, with Barry positioned just behind Erling Haaland in the goalscoring chart.
summary: Thierno Barry scored two goals to help Everton secure a comeback victory against Coventry. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added a late goal to seal Everton's third consecutive win.

content:

The squad is currently dealing with significant absences due to injuries sustained on the Bagshot training pitch. Tom Curry, Alex Mitchell, and Archie McParland are all out, while Guy Pepper, Benhard van Rensburg, Sam Underhill, Kepu Tuipulotu, and Chandler Cunningham-South are also unavailable. These missing players have left the team with less energy and dynamism than expected.

The piece suggests that Sunday’s hosts must stop seeking excuses and instead focus on what they can control. As crowds gather at Twickenham, uncertainty remains about what to expect from the match, with the team preparing to face a battle-hardened Australian side.
summary: England's squad is missing several key players, including Tom Curry, Alex Mitchell, and Archie McParland, due to injuries sustained on the training pitch. title: Mother and baby's immune cells linked to aggressive placental inflammation in preterm cases
content:
Researchers led by Nardhy Gomez-Lopez, a professor of obstetrics and gynecology and of pathology and immunology at WashU Medicine, investigated the cellular drivers of chronic placental inflammation. This condition can occur when the maternal immune response, which typically prevents fetal rejection, becomes dysregulated. The study specifically examined the immune cell landscape at the junction connecting the mother and fetus in pregnancies affected by this complication.

To map these immune cells, the team utilized spatial and single-cell gene and protein expression profiling. This approach allowed them to analyze the placenta down to individual cells, providing detailed insights into the aggressive inflammation associated with preterm cases.
summary: In a healthy pregnancy, a finely tuned maternal immune response prevents the mother's body from rejecting the growing fetus. But in some pregnancies, this response goes haywire, leading to a potentially dangerous complication known as chronic placental inflammation.

title: MIT's CheMeleon model predicts molecular behavior from scant data
content:
A new method developed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) demonstrates that artificial intelligence can outperform existing approaches for predicting molecular behavior when data on specific properties is limited. This development addresses the trial-and-error nature of discovering new molecules for pharmaceuticals, electronics, and energy sectors, where perfect prediction of chemical compound behavior remains elusive. The findings were published in the Sept. 14 issue of the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling by MIT graduate student Akshat Shirish Zalte, recent graduate Jackson Burns PhD ’26, Research Scientist Charlles Abreu, Professor William Green, and three researchers from BASF.

The open-source model, named CheMeleon, was built using ChemProp, a machine-learning package developed and maintained by the Green group at MIT. CheMeleon is a pre-trained foundation model that utilizes molecular descriptors of one million molecules from PubChem, a freely available chemical database maintained by the U.S. National Institutes of Health. By pre-training on this extensive dataset, the model learns correlations between molecular structure and a catalog of approximately 1,600 descriptors developed by chemists. This process allows the system to identify underlying patterns and relationships, enabling it to apply this general chemical understanding to new, unknown molecules even when fine-tuned with only a few data points for a specific task.

Professor William Green, the Hoyt Hottel Professor of Chemical Engineering at MIT, noted the model’s impact following a contest organized by OpenADMET earlier this year to predict properties of unsynthesized molecules. When the winners were announced, nine of the top 20 entries had utilized CheMeleon in their process. This success led to inquiries from pharmaceutical companies before the paper had even undergone peer review. Green stated that at least one pharmaceutical company adopted CheMeleon as its new company policy for initial molecular modeling decisions, instructing its staff to start with the tool when modeling any property.

Akshat Shirish Zalte explained that unlike many deep-learning models that require extensive data from published literature, CheMeleon does not rely on literature sources. Instead, it calculates molecular descriptors such as molecular weight and the number of oxygens. The team compared CheMeleon against other foundation models and classical expert-driven models across 58 test cases. Zalte reported that CheMeleon performed best in these comparisons. Green added that the model drastically reduces the number of molecules requiring experimental testing, offering a significant advantage given that synthesizing and testing large numbers of molecules is both slow and expensive.

The research team included Jochen Sieg, Christian Feldmann, and Miriam Mathea, researchers at BASF SE in Germany. The work was supported by the Machine Learning for Pharmaceutical Discovery and Synthesis consortium, as well as fellowship support from the U.S. Department of Energy and MathWorks. An earlier version of the paper has been available online since last year, and the model is accessible for download and fine-tuning through ChemProp.
summary: Researchers at MIT developed CheMeleon, a pre-trained foundation model that uses molecular descriptors from a million compounds to predict chemical properties with high accuracy. The open-source model outperformed other methods in 58 test cases and has been adopted by pharmaceutical companies to reduce the number of molecules requiring expensive experimental testing.

title: Is 'ferritin face' real? Experts explain iron deficiency signs
content: Social media is awash with claims iron deficiency can be identified in the mirror by dark circles, breaking hair and dry skin. But is ‘ferritin face’ real? Madeleine Finlay tells Ian Sample why so many of us struggle to keep our iron levels up, how we can actually diagnose low iron and the best way to correct a deficiency, with help from Hal Drakesmith, a professor of iron biology at Oxford University, and advice from Dr Sue Pavord, a consultant haematologist at Oxford university hospitals and associate senior lecturer in clinical medicine at St Edmund Hall.
summary: Social media claims that iron deficiency causes dark circles, hair loss, and dry skin, but experts question if this 'ferritin face' is real. Madeleine Finlay discusses how to diagnose and correct low iron with help from Oxford University professors and consultants.

title: LDraw Mecha: Agents Infer LEGO Mechanisms from Source and Animate Them
content:
A developer has released LDraw Mecha, a new agentic tool designed to animate LEGO models by inferring their mechanical structures from source code. The project builds on the creator’s previous release, LDraw Nova, which generates LDraw source code for assembling LEGO CAD models. Following community interest in animated AI-generated LEGO models, the developer explored using agentic large language models to reverse-engineer mechanisms within existing LDraw files.

LDraw Mecha operates by reading specially annotated LDraw source files to infer the model’s structure and identify specific submodels that function as mechanisms. The system then plans animations for these components and executes them using Blender. The final output is a rigged and animated version of the original model, exported as a Blender (.blend) file.

The project is currently at version 0.5.0, with a public repository, gallery, and process documentation available on GitHub. The creator has shared the work on Hacker News, seeking community feedback on this unusual application of agentic AI in 3D animation.
summary: Hi there :) Around a month ago, I released LDraw Nova, an agentic toolset for assembling LEGO CAD models by generating LDraw source code files. For more details, here's the Show HN post: https://news.

title: AI data center expansion faces bipartisan backlash, polls, and new regulatory restrictions
content:
Massive new data centers serve as the physical foundation for the artificial intelligence ambitions of major technology companies, yet their rapid expansion has sparked global conflicts regarding power grids, utility bills, and environmental impacts. Data centers emerged as a significant bipartisan issue ahead of the 2026 midterms, with voters largely opposing expansion at the polls. In the aftermath of the election, Democratic leaders are calling for further restrictions and slowdowns, while tech giants like OpenAI and Amazon promise to collaborate more closely with local communities and cover their own energy costs.

The political landscape surrounding these facilities has shifted dramatically, with data centers influencing the outcome of several key races. Maine Republican Susan Collins conceded her Senate seat in a tech-fueled race, while a Democrat was projected to win an Ohio seat that Republicans warned could pose problems for data center development. Additionally, Texas, a state dense with data centers, turned blue in the election. Following these results, a lame-duck Congress is considering measures to speed up energy projects, while New York became the first state to enact a data center moratorium.

Environmental and community concerns have intensified, with reports indicating that data centers could send US climate pollution skyrocketing and erase decades of air quality gains. Specific regions are facing distinct challenges; for instance, AI infrastructure is straining Arizona’s water supply, and Amazon’s data centers used 2.5 billion gallons of water last year. In Utah, a 40,000-acre data center project was approved despite community outcry, and Kevin O’Leary agreed to downsize a massive project in the state. Meanwhile, in Indiana, the mayor of Shelbyville stated that only people living in “shitty houses” oppose data centers, while Amazon employees have reported facing termination for backing data center limits.

Tech companies are responding to these pressures through various strategic moves. OpenAI has begun renaming its facilities “compute campuses” and is stepping back from non-disclosure agreements for its projects. Nvidia has guaranteed up to $105 billion to support an OpenAI data center, while Anthropic is paying $15 billion a year for access to Elon Musk’s data centers. Other major players, including Google, Meta, and Microsoft, are pursuing diverse energy solutions, such as nuclear power, geothermal energy, and vehicle-to-grid technology, to manage the immense power demands of their infrastructure.

The debate has also extended to unconventional locations and infrastructure. Elon Musk has proposed merging SpaceX and xAI to build data centers in space, a concept Google and Amazon have also explored. On the ground, the construction boom has led to a surge in gas projects to power data centers, with the Department of Justice arguing that XAI’s gas-powered facility is necessary for national security. As the industry expands, utility companies are promising to spare consumers from the full cost of AI’s energy bill, while regulators in California and other states tighten rules on energy and water usage.
summary: Voters largely opposed data center expansion in the 2026 midterms, leading Democratic leaders to call for further restrictions and slowdowns. Tech companies are responding by promising to cover energy costs and work more closely with local communities.

content: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth. As part of its plans to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, SpaceX has inked a deal with Qualcomm, which will deploy its cellular technology across tens of thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. SpaceX is also reportedly in talks to buy Boost Mobile, potentially allowing it to launch Starlink Mobile through the service. Another report suggests SpaceX may tap into 80,000 cell sites across the US to build out its network. SpaceX’s big plans have garnered some reactions in the telecom industry. title: AST SpaceMobile to Develop Medium‑Lift Rocket Blacklift to Expand Market
content: There are optimistic plans for spaceflight, and then there are optimistic plans. AST SpaceMobile is a Texas-based, publicly traded company building very large satellites to provide direct-to-cell communications on Earth. But it has been having trouble finding rides to space. So on Friday, AST announced that it is developing a medium-lift rocket, named Blacklift, which will have the capacity to lift 20 metric tons to low-Earth orbit. Oh, and the company said it would start launching commercially in late 2028. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owner's economics in the industry," said Abel Avellan, founder, chairman, and CEO of AST SpaceMobile, in a news release. Read full article Comments

title: John Wick creator Chad Stahelski returns with dystopian action film Karōshi
content: Those of us missing the John Wick universe can take heart, because Chad Stahelski—who created that franchise—is coming back early next year with a new dystopian action film. It's called Karōshi (a Japanese term that means "death overwork"), and Lionsgate released a killer trailer that puts this film at the top of my list of "must see" movies of 2027. Dying from working too hard is a very real phenomenon, not just in Japan and much of Asia, but also in Sweden. The physical cause is usually stress-related heart attacks or strokes, as well as suicide ( karōjisatsu in Japan). Writer/director Takashi Doscher has transported that concept to a grim, futuristic corporate Manhattan, specifically a company called Ikigai Technologies. Per the official premise: Karōshi is an action-thriller set in a near-future Manhattan, where corporate loyalty and cultural tradition have reshaped everyday life. When a mysterious outsider infiltrates a powerful company after a worker’s death, he exposes the violent system hidden beneath its polished surface. Teo Yoo ( Past Lives ) stars as the aptly named Hiro, who is clearly out for vengeance against the offending corporation. The cast also includes Takehiro Hira, so memorable in the 2024 miniseries Shōgun, as well as Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu. Read full article Comments
summary: Chad Stahelski, creator of the John Wick franchise, is returning with the dystopian action film Karōshi, set in a near‑future Manhattan corporate environment. The film, written and directed by Takashi Doscher, stars Teo Yoo, Takehiro Hira, Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu.

title: FAA to ditch floppy disks in historic air traffic control upgrade
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration announced that it will discontinue the use of floppy disks in its air‑traffic control system. The agency said the move is part of a long‑awaited modernization effort that will give controllers faster access to data needed for safety alerts.

The upgrade involves installing the new Enterprise Information Display System (E‑IDS) in 435 facilities, replacing several older information display systems that date back to the 1980s. According to the FAA, the new system will replace floppy disks that hold vital weather and other critical information with a streamlined, 21st‑century solution.

E‑IDS will be deployed to operational control positions at more than 400 facilities across all air‑traffic control domains. The FAA said the system will provide operationally essential information for controlling aircraft.
summary: The FAA will stop using floppy disks as part of a long‑awaited upgrade that will give air‑traffic controllers faster access to safety‑alert data. The new Enterprise Information Display System will be installed in 435 facilities, replacing older display systems that date to the 1980s.

title: Nvidia hardware worth $11.4 M disappears en route from Oakland to Texas
content:
A shipment of Nvidia hardware worth $11.4 million disappeared while being transported from Oakland to Texas. According to The Mercury News, six pallets of unknown Nvidia equipment left Oakland on August 29 in a truck bound for Fort Worth, Texas. The truck, bearing the logo of a food‑transportation company, was scheduled to pick up the cargo and then vanish from the grid.

The theft was not discovered until early September, when the buyers realized the shipment had never arrived. Police tracing the truck’s route found it made several multi‑hour stops after picking up the hardware before the vehicle was lost somewhere in San Bernardino County, California.

Oakland police confirmed that a grand theft report was filed on September 13 and that the investigation remains ongoing. Authorities have not disclosed the specific Nvidia hardware that was stolen or the exact method of the theft.
summary: Nvidia hardware worth $11.4 M disappears en route from Oakland to Texas.

title: Earth's Mantle Movements May Explain Great Unconformity Gap
content: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. Read full article Comments
summary: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top.
author: Ars Technica

title: Chainalysis reports hackers stole credentials and tokens for all customers
content:
Chainalysis, a blockchain analysis firm, announced that hackers have obtained sensitive personal information for all of its users following a breach of its network security. The stolen data includes names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens. The firm listed a number of high‑profile customers, such as the FBI, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the U.S. Air Force, Microsoft, Coinbase, and Barclays. It is unclear whether the theft exposes these customers to additional threats.

The company said the incident occurred in October and was similar to other hacks that month. An external actor used AI‑agent‑assisted offensive techniques to gain unauthorized access to Chainalysis systems and internal tools. In an email to affected customers, Chainalysis noted that “non‑sensitive customer data, such as user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels for users provisioned on our platform were accessed.” The firm has not explained why it classified this information as non‑sensitive.
summary: Chainalysis said hackers obtained names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all its users after a breach. The incident, which used AI‑agent‑assisted techniques, impacted customers such as the FBI, ICE, US Air Force, Microsoft, Coinbase and Barclays.
author: Ars Technica

title: OpenAI reportedly raises additional $11B in funding round
content: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion in a funding round that has not yet closed. The round is expected to close in the coming weeks, and the company’s valuation is reported at $1.25 trillion.
summary: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion. The funding round has not yet closed but is expected to close in the coming weeks.
